2:177.ar: ۞لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَٰهَدُواْۖ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ
2:177.en: It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West; but righteous is he who believeth in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Scripture and the prophets; and giveth wealth, for love of Him, to kinsfolk and to orphans and the needy and the wayfarer and to those who ask, and to set slaves free; and observeth proper worship and payeth the poor-due. And those who keep their treaty when they make one, and the patient in tribulation and adversity and time of stress. Such are they who are sincere. Such are the Allah-fearing

2:214.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۖ مَّسَّتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءُ وَٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ مَتَىٰ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ نَصۡرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبࣱ‏
2:214.en: Or think ye that ye will enter paradise while yet there hath not come unto you the like of (that which came to) those who passed away before you? Affliction and adversity befell them, they were shaken as with earthquake, till the messenger (of Allah) and those who believed along with him said: When cometh Allah's help? Now surely Allah's help is nigh

2:246.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَلَإِ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذۡ قَالُواْ لِنَبِيࣲّ لَّهُمُ ٱبۡعَثۡ لَنَا مَلِكࣰ ا نُّقَٰتِلۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ هَلۡ عَسَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ أَلَّا تُقَٰتِلُواْۖ قَالُواْ وَمَا لَنَآ أَلَّا نُقَٰتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَدۡ أُخۡرِجۡنَا مِن دِيَٰرِنَا وَأَبۡنَآئِنَاۖ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوۡاْ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:246.en: Bethink thee of the leaders of the Children of Israel after Moses, how they said unto a prophet whom they had: Set up for us a king and we will fight in Allah's way. He said: Would ye then refrain from fighting if fighting were prescribed for you? They said: Why should we not fight in Allah's way when we have been driven from our dwellings with our children? Yet, when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, all save a few of them. Allah is aware of evil-doers

2:247.ar: وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ نَبِيُّهُمۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ بَعَثَ لَكُمۡ طَالُوتَ مَلِكࣰ اۚ قَالُوٓاْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ عَلَيۡنَا وَنَحۡنُ أَحَقُّ بِٱلۡمُلۡكِ مِنۡهُ وَلَمۡ يُؤۡتَ سَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلۡمَالِۚ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَزَادَهُۥ بَسۡطَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ وَٱلۡجِسۡمِۖ وَٱللَّهُ يُؤۡتِي مُلۡكَهُۥ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:247.en: Their Prophet said unto them: Lo! Allah hath raised up Saul to be a king for you. They said: How can he have kingdom over us when we are more deserving of the kingdom than he is, since he hath not been given wealth enough? He said: Lo! Allah hath chosen him above you, and hath increased him abundantly in wisdom and stature. Allah bestoweth His Sovereignty on whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing

2:248.ar: وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ نَبِيُّهُمۡ إِنَّ ءَايَةَ مُلۡكِهِۦٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلتَّابُوتُ فِيهِ سَكِينَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَبَقِيَّةࣱ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ءَالُ مُوسَىٰ وَءَالُ هَٰرُونَ تَحۡمِلُهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
2:248.en: And their Prophet said unto them: Lo! the token of his kingdom is that there shall come unto you the ark wherein is peace of reassurance from your Lord, and a remnant of that which the house of Moses and the house of Aaron left behind, the angels bearing it. Lo! herein shall be a token for you if (in truth) ye are believers

2:249.ar: فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلۡجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبۡتَلِيكُم بِنَهَرࣲ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنۡهُ فَلَيۡسَ مِنِّي وَمَن لَّمۡ يَطۡعَمۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّيٓ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱغۡتَرَفَ غُرۡفَةَۢ بِيَدِهِۦۚ فَشَرِبُواْ مِنۡهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡۚ فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُۥ هُوَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ قَالُواْ لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ ٱللَّهِ كَم مِّن فِئَةࣲ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةࣰ كَثِيرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
2:249.en: And when Saul set out with the army, he said: Lo! Allah will try you by (the ordeal of) a river. Whosoever therefore drinketh thereof he is not of me, and whosoever tasteth it not he is of me, save him who taketh (thereof) in the hollow of his hand. But they drank thereof, all save a few of them. And after he had crossed (the river), he and those who believed with him, they said: We have no power this day against Goliath and his hosts. But those who knew that they would meet Allah exclaimed: How many a little company hath overcome a mighty host by Allah's leave! Allah is with the steadfast

2:250.ar: وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ قَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرࣰ ا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:250.en: And when they went into the field against Goliath and his hosts they said: Our Lord! Bestow on us endurance, make our foothold sure, and give us help against the disbelieving folk

2:251.ar: فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُۥدُ جَالُوتَ وَءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَعَلَّمَهُۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُۗ وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضࣲ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:251.en: So they routed them by Allah's leave and David slew Goliath; and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom, and taught him of that which He willeth. And if Allah had not repelled some men by others the earth would have been corrupted. But Allah is a Lord of Kindness to (His) creatures

8:15.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا لَقِيتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ زَحۡفࣰ ا فَلَا تُوَلُّوهُمُ ٱلۡأَدۡبَارَ
8:15.en: O ye who believe! When ye meet those who disbelieve in battle, turn not your backs to them

8:16.ar: وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ دُبُرَهُۥٓ إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفࣰ ا لِّقِتَالٍ أَوۡ مُتَحَيِّزًا إِلَىٰ فِئَةࣲ فَقَدۡ بَآءَ بِغَضَبࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَأۡوَىٰهُ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
8:16.en: Whoso on that day turneth his back to them, unless manoeuvring for battle or intent to join a company, he truly hath incurred wrath from Allah, and his habitation will be hell, a hapless journey's end

39:10.ar: قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡۚ لِلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣱۗ وَأَرۡضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةٌۗ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ أَجۡرَهُم بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
39:10.en: Say: O My bondmen who believe! Observe your duty to your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good, and Allah's earth is spacious. Verily the steadfast will be paid their wages without stint

IfXkn__hm9g.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 2: Quranic Themes, Perseverance
IfXkn__hm9g.one_line: Sabr as active perseverance toward a goal, tested at the moment of shock, through 2:177, 2:214 and the story of Talut and Jalut.
IfXkn__hm9g.summary: He explains that each night takes one of roughly a hundred underlying Quranic themes, the canvas beneath every surah, and tonight's is perseverance. Life is either ease that calls for gratitude or difficulty that calls for sabr, so perseverance is half of faith. He separates it from passive forbearance, since it requires a goal pursued through obstacles, and from mujahadah, the lifelong striving it serves. In 2:177 righteousness is not merely facing a direction in prayer but deep faith, giving wealth out of love, real prayer and zakat, and keeping one's word, with the perseverant singled out grammatically and three moments named: hardship, harm and the decisive moment. The woman who objected at her loss and then apologised shows that sabr is tested at the first shock. Verse 2:214 corrects the assumption of entering Paradise untested; Allah's help is near, but real change takes decades and we may not see it, just as the Prophet did not see Islam spread across three continents. Khabbab's plea from the burning coals drew a firm reply. The story of Talut shows an army shrinking with every test until a small persevering core, with Dawud, defeats Jalut. Hard moments are earned opportunities, and the perseverant are rewarded without reckoning.

outline.heading: Opening
Underlying themes: the canvas of the Quran
outline.gist: Beyond each surah's own objective, around a hundred themes such as purpose, accountability and death run through the whole Quran; learning them makes each surah easier to understand, and any theme can be found in any night's verses.

outline.heading: Half of faith: no third state
outline.gist: Perseverance is half of one's relationship with Allah because a person is always either in ease, which calls for gratitude, or in some difficulty, which calls for sabr; feeling neutral is simply ease one fails to acknowledge.

outline.heading: Sabr is active, forbearance is passive
outline.gist: Forbearance is controlling your reaction to others' bad behaviour, a beautiful trait and a name of Allah, while perseverance requires an objective you pursue through obstacles.

outline.heading: Sabr and mujahadah
outline.gist: Sabr is what you show in the moment of a particular difficulty, while mujahadah is the umbrella term for a lifestyle of continuous striving in every lane of life.

outline.heading: Righteousness is not facing east or west
outline.gist: For Medina facing the qiblah meant facing south; prayer is an obligation, but treating it as the only virtue or the one that trumps all others misses what true righteousness is.

outline.heading: Righteousness: deep faith
outline.gist: It starts with a deep acknowledgement of Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the books and the prophets.

outline.heading: Righteousness: giving wealth out of love
outline.gist: For the love of Allah one gives to relatives, orphans, the poor, travellers, those who ask and those in bondage, all people lacking financial stability.

outline.heading: Righteousness: prayer and zakat established properly
outline.gist: Prayer is established as it should be, not just its movements, and wealth is given as due.

outline.heading: Righteousness: keeping your word
outline.gist: Those who make a covenant see it through; the verse spans belief, ethics, ritual and behaviour.

outline.heading: Perseverance when it matters most
outline.gist: For many companions the decisive moment was battle, which is why the Quran forbids turning one's back to the enemy; for us it may be poverty, harm for our faith or discrimination, and failing then undoes years of perseverance.

outline.heading: Sabr is at the first shock
outline.gist: A grieving woman answered the Prophet's consolation with words of objection, then ran to apologise when she learned who he was; true perseverance shows at the moment of impact, though repentance afterwards always helps.

outline.heading: Hardship: when it is tight
outline.gist: Sometimes there is no harm, just difficulty: not making ends meet, goals failing.

outline.heading: Harm: when people hurt you
outline.gist: Sometimes people are actively trying to harm you, and you persevere through it.

outline.heading: The moment of truth
outline.gist: No one knows when the decisive moment will come, so cultivate now the wish to be ready and not lose your composure when it matters most.

outline.heading: The grammar that singles out the perseverant
outline.gist: Every other quality is listed in the same case, but 'the perseverant' switches case, which in Arabic means 'and I especially single out this group'; at the moment of shock, let only praise be on your tongue and fall in prostration.

outline.heading: Ask for ease, and for strength if tested
outline.gist: His teacher used to ask Allah not to keep testing him because he was weak; we ask for lives of ease and, if tested, strength at the moment of difficulty.

outline.heading: Did you think you would enter Paradise untested?
outline.gist: The verse corrects a mistaken assumption with a rhetorical question; it is rarely discussed in depth because it imposes a reality many would rather not believe, and the Quran repeats it in several forms.

outline.heading: Shaken to the core
outline.gist: Those before us met hardship and harm, the same two words as 2:177, and were shaken as if by an earthquake of trials until the messenger and believers asked when Allah's help would come.

outline.heading: Help is near, but we measure wrongly
outline.gist: We expect change in months or a couple of years, but real change takes decades of work.

outline.heading: You may not live to see the result
outline.gist: Whoever starts solving a real problem will probably not see the outcome and must accept that; the Prophet died at around sixty-one solar years, before Islam spread across three continents within two decades.

outline.heading: Khabbab on the burning coals
outline.gist: An early Muslim slave and skilled blacksmith buying his freedom was laid by bullies on his own bed of live coals until the fat of his back put them out, and came to the Prophet on all fours asking how long this would last.

outline.heading: The Prophet's firm answer
outline.gist: Sensing a trace of objection, the Prophet, usually the one who comforted everyone, told him that believers before were sawn in half without leaving their faith, that Allah would make this message prevail, but that they were impatient.

outline.heading: No sugarcoating the verse
outline.gist: This is what the verse says: Paradise comes after hardship, harm and the moment one almost says the wrong thing but turns back to Allah; His help is always near, and our job is to hold on.

outline.heading: Talut: chosen without lineage or wealth
outline.gist: The story appears only here in the Quran; Talut came from the wrong tribe and was not rich, but was strong and knowledgeable, and the people objected that he was not wealthy enough to be king.

outline.heading: An army that shrinks with every test
outline.gist: The people had asked their prophet Samuel for a king to reclaim the holy land, then backed out; only about a tenth went, a further nine tenths fell away at each test, leaving about 314, the number at Badr.

outline.heading: The river test
outline.gist: They were told not to drink from the river except a handful; all but a few drank, the Arabic word for few implying around a tenth, and those who drank were sent home.

outline.heading: How many a small band has overcome a great one
outline.gist: After crossing, some said they had no strength against Jalut and his army, while those certain of meeting Allah said small groups often defeat large ones by His will, and Allah is with the perseverant.

outline.heading: Tests move you closer or farther
outline.gist: The story mirrors our lives: every obstacle takes us a step toward Allah or away from Him, and one can always redeem oneself.

outline.heading: The hardest moment is an earned opportunity
outline.gist: Standing before Goliath was a gift earned through earlier perseverance; our most difficult moments solidify our legacy and are what we will plead with on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: The people of Badr were chosen
outline.gist: Those present at Badr were selected by Allah, which is why companions who missed it, even for innocent reasons, felt the loss and made sure to attend every battle after.

outline.heading: Pour perseverance upon us
outline.gist: The underdog story became part of world culture; facing a larger, stronger army that may end your life is the hardest thing, so they asked Allah to empty all perseverance upon them and make their feet firm.

outline.heading: Dawud kills Jalut and the balance changes
outline.gist: A people living hopeless on the edge of the holy land went on to a lasting kingdom; Allah can change the balance at any time.

outline.heading: Enough people must hold
outline.gist: Had only Talut and Dawud refused to drink they would have had to turn back; a small but sufficient core that perseveres when it matters is what brings victory.

outline.heading: Which side of the story will you be on?
outline.gist: The story repeats throughout history: one can quit when the king is named, at the river, or at the sight of the enemy, or persevere and be granted the moment that pleads for one's sins.

outline.heading: Reward without reckoning
outline.gist: The perseverant are given their reward without account, a fast track to Paradise with no questions asked.

GAUkRtImKcQ.speaker: adnan
GAUkRtImKcQ.speaker_note: continues his own Tazkiyah Pearls series and recounts his own training with a teacher
GAUkRtImKcQ.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 2: Origins, Rules and Nomenclature
GAUkRtImKcQ.one_line: Where the science of tazkiyah comes from, the rules for studying it, and key terms: ruh, nafs, hawa, the heart, consciousness and intellect.
GAUkRtImKcQ.summary: He traces tazkiyah to the Prophet's teaching that the body is sound when the heart is sound, and explains that, like hadith and the qira'at, it became a formal discipline in the first centuries, built on emulating the Prophet, eating lawfully and purifying intention, and documented by early scholars up to al-Ghazali. The Quran lists purification among the core purposes of prophethood. He then sets the rules of study. Above all, everything learned applies to yourself, never projected onto spouses, children or others, who should be seen with compassion. It also demands reflection, sincere exercises such as serving someone you dislike or making dua for someone you envy, and a committed daily portion of Quran and dhikr built up gradually. Finally he defines terms: the ruh is the elevated self from Allah; the nafs, born when spirit met body, is a survival-driven, well-meaning child that fears death; hawa is its desires, which can be aligned with the Prophet's teaching; the heart works like a subconscious melting pot shaped slowly by what we pour in; consciousness is live awareness; and the intellect processes information and steers the heart, so how we interpret others changes how we feel.

outline.heading: The heart that sets the whole body right
outline.gist: The Prophet taught that when the heart is sound the whole body is sound; that raises what the heart is, how to purify it and what is at risk.

outline.heading: Islamic disciplines formed after the Prophet
outline.gist: Qira'at, hadith and other sciences took a century or more to take form because the companions simply emulated the Prophet directly.

outline.heading: Following a teacher still works today
outline.gist: Not everyone must be a scholar, but each person needs someone to learn from, and wider Islamic literacy benefits the community.

outline.heading: The foundations and classical books of tazkiyah
outline.gist: Early scholars built it on emulating the Prophet's ethics, eating lawfully and pure intention, and wrote the works on asceticism and the heart, most famously al-Ghazali's.

outline.heading: Purification as a purpose of prophethood
outline.gist: The Quran says the Prophet was sent to recite Allah's signs, purify people and teach the Book and wisdom; Allah reordered Ibrahim's dua to place purification earlier.

outline.heading: Learn tazkiyah from its specialists
outline.gist: Just as one learns hadith from hadith scholars, this knowledge should be taken from those who specialise in it.

outline.heading: Rule: it is all about you
outline.gist: Apply every lesson to yourself and see others with compassion; projecting it onto family or others ruins relationships and multiplies your sins, unless someone asks you to mentor them.

outline.heading: Rule: everything requires reflection
outline.gist: Hearing a concept does not make it second nature; it takes time and contemplation to become meaningful.

outline.heading: Rule: sincere exercises
outline.gist: His teacher had him serve a Muslim he disliked, which took him three weeks; making dua for someone you envy teaches you about your nafs.

outline.heading: Rule: a committed daily portion of Quran
outline.gist: The Prophet had companions keep a daily portion and make it up the next morning if missed; treat a chosen commitment as if it were obligatory.

outline.heading: The hadith of drawing near through voluntary deeds
outline.gist: Allah's servant draws near through voluntary deeds until Allah loves him and becomes his hearing, sight and refuge; that is the goal of the daily routine.

outline.heading: Building up daily dhikr gradually
outline.gist: One of his teachers did ten thousand dhikr a day; start with what you can, add a hundred at a time over years until the tongue never stops.

outline.heading: Becoming sensitive to the voice of the nafs
outline.gist: Exercises teach you to recognise the nafs resisting; its reluctance and rationalising are often a sign you should do the thing anyway.

outline.heading: Term: the ruh
outline.gist: The spirit Allah breathed into Adam is the elevated self behind empathy, hope and metacognition; it is not from this universe and simply moves on at death.

outline.heading: Term: the nafs as a survival-driven cheerleader
outline.gist: Born from spirit and body, the nafs starts out commanding wrong, loves you and wants you on top of the food chain, but does not know what is good for you.

outline.heading: The nafs is like a three-year-old
outline.gist: Worrying about food shares or grabbing a toy only because another child has it is the unfiltered nafs, funny at three and ugly at thirty; we love it but do not follow it.

outline.heading: The nafs fears death and must be tamed
outline.gist: The nafs ends with the body, so it fears death while the ruh does not; it is a wild horse to be tamed.

outline.heading: Term: hawa, the desires of the nafs
outline.gist: Food, sex, status, wealth and dominance are its wants; true faith comes when hawa follows the Prophet's teaching, so the nafs itself pulls you to the masjid.

outline.heading: The Prophet's tamed nafs and his standard
outline.gist: What the Quran corrects in the Prophet would count as good deeds for us; his nafs led him to Allah. Nafs, ego and soul are used interchangeably.

outline.heading: Term: the heart as a subconscious melting pot
outline.gist: Everything seen, heard, thought and experienced pours into the heart and comes out as feelings: garbage in, garbage out.

outline.heading: The heart is controlled indirectly over time, like HbA1c
outline.gist: Like a three-month blood sugar marker, the heart reflects what has been poured in for a while, and changes slowly.

outline.heading: Term: consciousness
outline.gist: Live awareness through the senses, the ability to take things in and choose from the moment you wake.

outline.heading: Term: the intellect steers the heart
outline.gist: The intellect processes information in real time and feeds the heart, so dwelling negatively on someone builds resentment; contemplation can end any dispute.

outline.heading: The driver who cut you off
outline.gist: Learning the driver's mother just died and his wife is in hospital changes your anger instantly, showing that reinterpretation changes feelings.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Tazkiyah developed like other Islamic sciences and should be learned from its specialists and classical works.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)

themes.label: Envy, anger and other diseases of the heart

themes.label: Dhikr: remembrance of Allah
themes.note: A committed daily portion of Quran and dhikr, built up gradually, is how one comes under Allah's love.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: The fear of death belongs to the nafs, not the ruh.

x8XA3BS399w.title: The Beauty of Ramadan: Ramadan Treasures (Kunuz Ramadaniyyah)
x8XA3BS399w.one_line: Unpacking the hadith of Salman on Ramadan, then five treasures of the month: forgiveness, freedom from the Fire, multiplied rewards, answered dua and Laylat al-Qadr.
x8XA3BS399w.summary: A yearly pre-Ramadan lesson meant to rouse people to host the month well. He presents the month as the one twelfth of life that Allah returns every year as a chance to recharge and change, then works through the long hadith of Salman al-Farisi about the Prophet's sermon at the end of Sha'ban, after explaining why its weak chain does not sink its accepted meaning. Each phrase becomes a lesson: fasting from the lawful should push you further from the forbidden, so a fast that keeps lying, foul speech and harm earns only hunger; obligations outweigh every voluntary act, so never trade Isha and Fajr in congregation for taraweeh; patience is rewarded without reckoning; chosen hunger teaches empathy for the forced hunger of the poor; provision grows through gratitude and perspective rather than a bigger balance; and Ramadan replaces a culture of eating with a culture of feeding others. He then lists the month's treasures: forgiveness of past sins through faith and seeking reward, freedom from the Fire granted every night to those who strive to stand out, rewards beyond counting with fasting's reward kept by Allah, much dua, and Laylat al-Qadr, which teaches that the worth of deeds lies in their quality, not their length.

outline.heading: Honouring the guest month
outline.gist: The yearly reminder aims to rouse people to host Ramadan properly; the companions prayed to reach it beforehand and for its acceptance afterward, making it the axis of their year.

outline.heading: Every rite of worship gathered in one month
outline.gist: Fasting, night prayer, charity and zakat al-fitr all meet in Ramadan, which brings together the worship Allah loves.

outline.heading: A yearly recharge for an empty heart
outline.gist: One month in twelve returns every year as a chance to change; he compares the heart before Ramadan to a phone on an empty battery that the month refills until the next one.

outline.heading: Allah singles out times and places
outline.gist: Ramadan is one of the gusts of mercy in time; as Allah honoured the three sacred mosques among places, He honoured the sacred months and above all Ramadan among times.

outline.heading: A weak chain does not mean a weak text
outline.gist: He grades the hadith of Salman as acceptable by its supporting routes: its meanings are authentic elsewhere even if its chain is weak, which is why his teacher loved narrating it.

outline.heading: Salman's hadith: the sermon at the end of Sha'ban
outline.gist: He narrates the Prophet's address listing Ramadan's features: an obligatory fast, voluntary night prayer, multiplied deeds, patience, consolation, increased provision and the reward of giving iftar.

outline.heading: A blessed month: obligatory fast, voluntary night prayer
outline.gist: Blessing is a special quality; the Prophet prayed at night in Ramadan but avoided leading it every night in congregation so it would not become obligatory, showing the line between fard and sunnah.

outline.heading: Leaving the lawful to stand further from the forbidden
outline.gist: If you give up lawful food, drink and intimacy, giving up the forbidden comes first; it makes no sense to leave the halal side of the red line only to cross it.

outline.heading: A fast that earns only hunger and thirst
outline.gist: Some fast and gain nothing but hunger and some pray at night and gain only fatigue; Allah has no need of a fast that keeps false speech and acting on it.

outline.heading: The shepherd near the preserve and human weakness
outline.gist: Keep away from doubtful matters as a shepherd keeps his flock from the boundary; the self is weak, which is why Islam closes doors such as a man and woman alone together.

outline.heading: No obscenity or wrongdoing: losing the reward of the fast
outline.gist: Ramadan moves you further from the line; Aisha described the Prophet as the most in control of himself, and foul words, shouting or insulting do not break the fast but destroy its reward.

outline.heading: 'I am fasting' is a reminder, not a threat
outline.gist: Saying 'I am fasting' when provoked should calm both parties and protect a purified state, not warn people that you are on edge.

outline.heading: Nothing equals the obligations
outline.gist: The day's fast is the greatest act of Ramadan; by the hadith qudsi nothing brings one closer than what Allah made obligatory, and a lifetime of taraweeh does not equal two obligatory rakat, while voluntary prayers earn His special love.

outline.heading: Do not trade Fajr in congregation for taraweeh
outline.gist: If forced to choose, pray Isha in congregation, sleep, and come back for Fajr rather than staying for taraweeh and missing Fajr.

outline.heading: The Ramadan offer: deeds multiplied
outline.gist: Any good deed in Ramadan counts as an obligation outside it and each obligation as seventy, so increase voluntary acts.

outline.heading: Month of patience: reward without reckoning
outline.gist: The patient are the group the Quran plainly promises reward without account, the highest hope of a believer.

outline.heading: Beautiful patience and rewarded tiredness
outline.gist: Patience can be content or resentful; the exhaustion of Ramadan is a beautiful tiredness because you know it is rewarded, even the nap taken from long night prayer.

outline.heading: Month of consolation: empathy needs imagination
outline.gist: You cannot show mercy to someone whose state you cannot imagine, which is why many fail people with mental illness, while those who have suffered pain console others readily.

outline.heading: Chosen hunger to feel forced hunger
outline.gist: The fasting person hungers by choice and so can feel those who hunger by force; on a planet full of food, a hungry child is evidence of others falling short.

outline.heading: Urging the feeding of the poor
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly condemns the one who does not urge feeding the poor; he advises imagining before iftar that there is no food for you or your children.

outline.heading: Provision grows through perspective
outline.gist: The same gift thrills a poor child and disappoints a rich one; Ramadan lowers your expectations and changes how you see what you have.

outline.heading: Same balance, more gratitude
outline.gist: The increase in provision is in meaning: the same savings that felt too little before Ramadan feel like a blessing after a month of hunger and reflection.

outline.heading: The danger of growing used to blessings
outline.gist: Familiarity with blessings ruined earlier nations who thought the earth was theirs to keep; Allah gives and withholds so people learn how to handle both.

outline.heading: Look to those below you, but still strive
outline.gist: Look at those with less so you do not belittle Allah's blessing, while still working to improve your situation with contentment rather than resentment.

outline.heading: Competing to feed others
outline.gist: Ramadan turns the greedy habit of wanting to be fed into a competition to feed others, like the destitute man in the Haram walking around with a few dates looking for someone to break his fast.

outline.heading: Eat to live, not live to eat
outline.gist: After a day of hunger the focus at Maghrib is turned to others; feeding even a sip of milk or one date earns forgiveness and freedom.

outline.heading: Preferring your brother at the iftar table
outline.gist: Feeding others takes nothing from your own reward; the sunnah is for two people to break each other's fast, an exercise in preferring others and being saved from the greed of the self.

outline.heading: Mercy, forgiveness and freedom from the Fire
outline.gist: Rather than dividing the month into thirds, the point is that the obedient believer moves constantly between Allah's mercy, forgiveness and release from the Fire.

outline.heading: Treasure one: forgiveness through faith and seeking reward
outline.gist: Fasting, night prayer and Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and seeking reward erase past sins; faith means fasting only because Allah commanded it, not for people, status or weight loss.

outline.heading: Feeling the weight of sin and a clean page
outline.gist: The believer feels sins like a mountain about to fall while the hypocrite brushes them off like a fly; even the Prophet felt a burden that weighed on his back, and forgiveness gives a fresh start.

outline.heading: Treasure two: freedom from the Fire every night
outline.gist: Allah frees people from the Fire every night, more in the last ten and most on Laylat al-Qadr, something only Arafah shares.

outline.heading: The night you are freed
outline.gist: The greatest night of a life is the one Allah declares you free, and the Generous never takes back His gift; it does not mean you will not sin, but that good wins out and you return quickly, so seek it every year.

outline.heading: Strive to stand out to be chosen
outline.gist: Allah chooses the most sincere and hardworking for release, so compete and distinguish yourself; the Quran's descriptions of the Fire show what is at stake.

outline.heading: The criminal who would ransom his children
outline.gist: Surah al-Ma'arij shows a man offering his children, spouse, brother, clan and all on earth to escape; he asks what that man's eyes must have seen.

outline.heading: Treasure three: rewards beyond counting
outline.gist: Deeds are multiplied beyond reckoning, and fasting is for Allah who rewards it Himself, because no one but Him watches whether you keep it.

outline.heading: A day missed without excuse is never recovered
outline.gist: A day of Ramadan broken without excuse must be made up, but its unique reward is lost for good, unlike a day missed with a valid excuse.

outline.heading: Treasure five: a month of answered dua
outline.gist: Make much dua, since this is the month of dua; all the preparation of the month is aimed at one night.

outline.heading: Treasure four: Laylat al-Qadr, quality over length
outline.gist: A thousand months, a full lifetime, compressed into one night teaches that deeds are measured by quality, not duration.

outline.heading: Outro

r_2hERtNqSo.title: Making This Year the Best Ramadan of Our Lives
r_2hERtNqSo.one_line: A week before Ramadan: renew your intention, treat Laylat al-Qadr as the deal of a lifetime, plan ahead, and beautify the month with good conduct.
r_2hERtNqSo.summary: One week before Ramadan, the sheikh repeats the instruction he gives every year: renew your intention and resolve that this will be the best Ramadan of your life, because no one knows whether they will see another. He frames a lifetime as roughly a thousand full moons, eighty-three years, and Ramadan as one moon worth more than all of them, since Allah measures by quality, not quantity. Laylat al-Qadr compresses a lifetime of worship into a single night, and the one deprived of it is the truly deprived. His central analogy: anyone promised a guaranteed million-dollar cheque for showing up an hour a day for a month would never miss a day, so skipping the last ten nights reveals what we actually prioritize and is almost rude to the One making the offer. He describes booking off the last two weeks of next year's Ramadan at work, asks people to stamp themselves as devoted to Allah like a waqf mushaf, delete time-wasting apps, and schedule their sleep. In the second khutbah he insists that Ramadan is beautified by conduct as much as worship: no fights over prayer spots or with cars at the masjid, since rituals never justify harming others.

outline.heading: Opening
One verse on every minbar
outline.gist: The fasting verse is being recited this week and next on every minbar in the world; he loves imagining billions of Muslims hearing the same verse about the gift a week away.

outline.heading: Renew your intention: the best Ramadan of your life
outline.gist: For ten years he has opened every Ramadan the same way: renew your intention and make this the best Ramadan of your life, even if you made the same intention every year before, because you do not know whether you will see the next one, or even this one.

outline.heading: Your life is a thousand full moons
outline.gist: A thousand months is over 83 years, about a full human life; what lies ahead is one of those thousand moons.

outline.heading: Quality, not quantity
outline.gist: This one moon is worth more than all the others together: Allah puts the most powerful things in the smallest creations and the most baraka in the smallest spans of time, and it can make up for the moons we wasted.

outline.heading: A night that can reset your life
outline.gist: Within this moon is a secret only Allah knows: a night that can fix your whole life, press reset on its negatives and let you turn a new page you can be proud of.

outline.heading: Gates opened, devils chained, a caller each night
outline.gist: On the first night of Ramadan the devils and the strongest of them are chained, every gate of Paradise opened and every gate of Hell closed, and a voice calls the seeker of good to come near and the seeker of evil to hold back.

outline.heading: The truly deprived one
outline.gist: Allah frees people from the Fire every night. In Musnad Ahmad: in this month is a night better than a thousand months, and whoever is deprived of its good is deprived of all good. The deprived one is not the poor person but the one who lived through those nights and took nothing, and will wish someone had shaken him awake.

outline.heading: Hidden to see who really cares
outline.gist: Allah could have pinpointed the night as He pinpointed the month; leaving it unclear has a reason, which an everyday analogy makes plain.

outline.heading: The million-dollar cheque
outline.gist: Promised a guaranteed million-dollar cheque on one of thirty days for showing up an hour or two, everyone would come every day; people gamble their lives away on far worse odds. He would show up, quit his job, invest half and treat patients for free.

outline.heading: A lifetime compressed into one night
outline.gist: Allah compressed 83 years of worship into one night: a thousand months is 30,000 days, so one night counts like 30,000. Not showing up for a guaranteed reward is a tell about your relationship with Allah: the reward does not matter enough to you.

outline.heading: Almost rude: gambling on the 27th
outline.gist: No one demands praying all night, but not bringing your best and taking a chance on the 27th alone is almost rude to the One making the offer. The question is priority: is His pleasure what you live for?

outline.heading: The Prophet did more in the last ten
outline.gist: Always a hard worker, he did far more in Ramadan than any other time and more in the last ten nights than the rest of Ramadan, because he knew what he wanted. Do we?

outline.heading: Plan ahead: the last ten already booked off
outline.gist: He has the last two weeks of Ramadan 2026 booked off at work, and colleagues think he is crazy. No beach is worth more than the last ten nights; just show up and receive the baraka coming down.

outline.heading: Now or never
outline.gist: Do we want it delivered to our homes while we sleep? This is the season: whatever you want to change, make the intention today, enter next Friday with it, and bring Allah the best version of yourself for Him to beautify.

outline.heading: Stamp yourself like a waqf mushaf
outline.gist: There will be mistakes and tired nights, but enter with intention. Like the stamp inside a mushaf saying it is devoted to Allah and cannot be sold, stamp yourself at the start of Ramadan; you have 990 other moons for everything else.

outline.heading: Real tawbah happens in Ramadan
outline.gist: Every story he knows of people who truly repented and found their connection with Allah happened in Ramadan, when He calls hearts and fills the masjid with faces unseen the rest of the year.

outline.heading: The month of the Quran
outline.gist: Ramadan outranks every month because Allah chose it for the Quran, first recited to the Prophet then. Read it alone and aloud, explain and contemplate it, practise it, and let love of it guide your life; the Prophet loved Ramadan.

outline.heading: Vacation time for worship
outline.gist: He prepared the Sahabah for the month and built them up for it. His new metric: things will get better once Muslims take vacation time, kept for beaches and cottages, to devote to Allah in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Dedicate the month back to Him
outline.gist: Allah dedicated this whole existence to you, so dedicate something to Him: intend more devotion than ever, attend every night you can and pray to the end, recite the Quran, drop bad habits.

outline.heading: Delete the apps and schedule your sleep
outline.gist: Delete the blue, green and orange apps and useless information, keep half an hour of news a night, and schedule when you sleep and rise. Turning down a thousand months in one night is like ignoring the deal on every billboard.

outline.heading: Interlude
Second khutbah: dress in the best ethics
outline.gist: Intend not only to be closer to Allah than ever but to wear the best manners this month: care for one another and the needs of those sitting beside you, not only the poor overseas who receive your money.

outline.heading: Rituals never at the expense of others
outline.gist: No fighting over spots or mistreating people at the entrance. Ramadan is beautified by worship and equally by conduct and empathy; praying every night while shoving your car into everyone's way earns less than staying home.

outline.heading: Outro

JbWpxOX7s0Q.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 1: Introduction to the Concept of Ihsan
JbWpxOX7s0Q.one_line: Why ihsan, the inner third of the deen, explains the gap between our worship and the companions', and why taming the nafs is the work of tazkiyah.
JbWpxOX7s0Q.summary: Opening a short morning series on tazkiyah, he starts from the hadith of Jibril: Islam is the outward practice, iman the belief system, and ihsan the inner dimension of worshipping Allah as if you see Him. Deeds need inner conditions for acceptance just as they need outward ones, and he argues this is what separated the companions from us: not the quantity of worship but its quality. The Prophet transformed harsh people into those who wept in night prayer, and Allah sent Musa to invite even Pharaoh to purify himself. Tazkiyah means purification, as in the Prophet's dua and in zakat. He then points to a universal gap between what we know is good, want and can do, and what we actually do, and names the barrier as the nafs. Surah Ash-Shams swears eleven oaths before declaring that success belongs to whoever purifies it, warning of deeds that weigh nothing. Drawing on the creation of Adam from soil and spirit, he describes the nafs as a second self holding the real steering wheel. He ends with a companion who kept reciting while struck by arrows, as an example of love, and invites listeners to start walking this path.

outline.heading: Opening
The hadith of Jibril: Islam, iman and ihsan
outline.gist: Faith has three compartments: outward actions, the belief system, and ihsan, defined as worshipping Allah as if you see Him, knowing He sees you.

outline.heading: Deeds need inner conditions as well as outward ones
outline.gist: Just as prayer needs correct timing, direction and purification, every deed has internal conditions for acceptance, and this is the domain of ihsan.

outline.heading: Quality, not quantity, separates us from the companions
outline.gist: We may have more time and even more deeds than the companions; the difference is the quality of their relationship with Allah, the Prophet's greatest accomplishment.

outline.heading: The Prophet transformed a harsh people
outline.gist: He came to people who saw emotion as weakness and some of whom buried daughters alive, and turned them into people who wept all night in prayer.

outline.heading: Umar's tear-stained cheeks
outline.gist: A man of great strength and strictness whose cheeks bore lines from years of night weeping; that inner fullness is why Islam spread so quickly.

outline.heading: Prayer as rest for the companions
outline.gist: We are Muslim by name but lack their experience; the Prophet sought rest in prayer and their prayers were far longer, yet they did not find them heavy.

outline.heading: Musa invites Pharaoh to purify himself
outline.gist: Even to a tyrant who enslaved and murdered, Allah sent Musa with an offer to help purify his heart.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah means purification: the Prophet's dua and zakat
outline.gist: The Prophet asked Allah to grant his nafs its taqwa and purify it; zakat carries the same meaning, removing what is no longer yours from your wealth.

outline.heading: Seeking refuge from useless knowledge and a hard heart
outline.gist: The Prophet sought refuge from knowledge that does not benefit, a heart without humility, an eye without tears and a nafs never satisfied, raising the question of why these happen.

outline.heading: The gap between knowing and doing
outline.gist: People know a deed like praying Fajr in the masjid is good, want it and can do it, yet do not, and most answer that they do not know why; that canyon needs explaining.

outline.heading: Surah Ash-Shams: eleven oaths for the nafs
outline.gist: Allah swears by sun, moon, day, night, sky and earth, all beyond our control, and then by the nafs, the one thing we can work on, to declare that whoever purifies it succeeds.

outline.heading: Deeds that weigh nothing
outline.gist: The one who neglects the nafs will be disappointed, watching deeds float like helium balloons on the scale because sincerity, humility and focus were missing.

outline.heading: Caring about the quality of deeds
outline.gist: No deed is perfect, but one who notices and keeps trying to fix it is very different from one who is complacent.

outline.heading: This knowledge comes from the Quran and Sunnah
outline.gist: Tazkiyah must be taken from those grounded in the sources; neglecting this third of the deen is why our faith keeps fluctuating.

outline.heading: Ramadan as a glimpse of what is possible
outline.gist: With one distraction removed, prayer and dua feel different in Ramadan; imagine feeling that most of the year.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah is a path, not an achievement
outline.gist: There is no moment of arrival; you keep walking the path until you die, even in baby steps.

outline.heading: The answers lie inside
outline.gist: We search outside for solutions that exist within; whoever tames himself can face anything, and whoever fails before his nafs fails before everything.

outline.heading: Adam made of soil and spirit
outline.gist: Unlike angels of light and jinn of smokeless fire, humans combine the earth's elements and instincts with a spirit from Allah, and from their meeting the nafs is born.

outline.heading: The nafs as a second self with the real steering wheel
outline.gist: The Quran speaks of purifying it, as if someone else is inside; it knows what it wants and lets you think you are in control like a child with an unplugged controller.

outline.heading: Most of the Quran teaches about the nafs
outline.gist: The Quran almost always explains why a command helps you, and its stories reflect something inside us to overcome.

outline.heading: Who is truly godly, and the Prophet's transforming presence
outline.gist: A young scholar defined the godly as one who speaks, stays silent and acts for Allah, selfless regarding his nafs; a glance or touch from the Prophet was enough to transform hearts.

outline.heading: The companion struck by arrows during prayer
outline.gist: He kept praying rather than cut his recitation short; that is not logic but love, and it is attainable.

outline.heading: Outro

2:281.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمࣰ ا تُرۡجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ

3:30.en: On the Day when every soul will find itself confronted with all that it hath done of good and all that it hath done of evil (every soul) will long that there might be a mighty space of distance between it and that (evil). 3:104.en: And there may spring from you a nation who invite to goodness, and enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency. Such are they who are successful

3:106.ar: يَوۡمَ تَبۡيَضُّ وُجُوهࣱ وَتَسۡوَدُّ وُجُوهࣱۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡوَدَّتۡ وُجُوهُهُمۡ أَكَفَرۡتُم بَعۡدَ إِيمَٰنِكُمۡ فَذُوقُواْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡفُرُونَ

iqu7m2Fnx4Y.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 3: Quranic Themes, Preparing for the Akhirah
iqu7m2Fnx4Y.one_line: Why the Quran describes Judgment Day: to make us prepare, through 2:281, deeds brought forward in 3:30, and the faces of 3:104-108.
iqu7m2Fnx4Y.summary: He distinguishes the Quran's underlying themes from each surah's own objective, then takes preparation for the Day of Judgment, a theme found in nearly every surah. The Quran describes that day to move us to prepare, not to supply verifiable details, but a generation raised on screen drama hears its scenes as spectators in a safe room; he urges listeners to place themselves in both the good and bad outcomes and use the emotion as fuel. Verse 2:281, which he promises to raise every year, was the last revelation: prepare for the day you return to Allah and are paid in full, a reminder not to overcomplicate faith. From 3:30 he describes every deed brought forward with nothing hidden, the shame of bad deeds, and Allah's warning of Himself, meaning one may meet His names of majesty rather than mercy; even the prophets will not dare intercede that day. From 3:104-108 he reads the call to good and the warning against division as addressed to the whole ummah, blaming its weakness on ego-driven disunity, and contrasts faces lit by Allah's mercy with faces darkened. He ends on the nature of that fear: we do not fear injustice from Allah but being dealt with strictly by justice, so we work to be worthy of His mercy.

outline.heading: Quranic themes versus surah objectives
outline.gist: Around a hundred themes form the background canvas of every surah; confusing them with a surah's own purpose makes people miss what each surah is saying, and every page of the Quran can yield all of them.

outline.heading: The point of describing Judgment Day
outline.gist: Most verses about the Day of Judgment aim at preparing for it; describing it is pointless if it does not lead to preparation.

outline.heading: Spectators of our own story
outline.gist: Raised on cartoons and cinema, we picture Quranic scenes as actors playing out a script and feel for them from the safety of home, while earlier generations projected the verses onto themselves.

outline.heading: Put yourself in both positions
outline.gist: Listen to the verses about those who succeeded and those who failed as if each were you, and let the feeling push you toward one and away from the other.

outline.heading: Emotion, not details, is the purpose
outline.gist: The details and even the sequence of the Hereafter cannot be verified and are not required for being Muslim; the repetition exists so that the emotion it generates moves you forward.

outline.heading: The motivation that gets you across the finish line
outline.gist: This motivation is built into the Quran to carry you to the end, and losing it holds you back; Ramadan's lack of distraction lets the verses sink in.

outline.heading: A theme in nearly every surah
outline.gist: Apart from a few very short surahs with a specific goal, every surah raises preparation for the Hereafter, most of them more than once.

outline.heading: The last verse revealed
outline.gist: He promises to raise this verse every year he is alive; it was the final revelation, standing alone among the verses on debts, and Jibril's next visit would bring the angel of death.

outline.heading: Taqwa as preparation
outline.gist: The root of taqwa means prevention and protection, which in practice means preparing beforehand so you do not walk into harm unprepared.

outline.heading: Returned to Allah and paid in full
outline.gist: We came from Allah, stay briefly, and return to Him to receive exactly what we earned, with no one wronged; what will you have to show for your time?

outline.heading: The shortest meeting with Jibril
outline.gist: Picture Jibril arriving with one verse, telling the Prophet where to place it and leaving at once; the Prophet knew it marked the end.

outline.heading: Don't overcomplicate your faith
outline.gist: If everything else feels too complicated, remember this: you will return to Allah soon to be compensated, so make sure you have deeds worthy of compensation and do not arrive empty-handed.

outline.heading: Every deed brought forward
outline.gist: Every soul will find the good it did presented before it, brought to the front, and likewise the evil.

outline.heading: Nothing can be hidden
outline.gist: In this life we keep both our good and bad deeds private, but that day everything is laid out, so the good had better outweigh the bad, and being seen by someone who knew you brings crushing shame.

outline.heading: Faces falling away in shame
outline.gist: Some will stand before Allah so ashamed when asked about their deeds that the flesh of their faces seems to fall off, a figure of how unbearable that shame is.

outline.heading: Wishing a great distance from one's sins
outline.gist: Every soul will wish its bad deeds were placed far away so it is no longer associated with them, while the good remain close.

outline.heading: Allah warns you of Himself
outline.gist: Repeated twice within a few verses, this may be the most fear-striking phrase in the Quran: alongside His names of beauty, Allah cautions you about Himself.

outline.heading: Facing the wrong set of names
outline.gist: Allah has names of majesty and might, and whoever makes the wrong choices may face those instead of the names of mercy that none of us can do without.

outline.heading: The wrath of the patient one
outline.gist: Which names you meet depends on what you bring; arriving with oppression, waste, ingratitude or discontent puts you in the line meant for oppressors, the name you want turned against those who wronged you.

outline.heading: Even the prophets will not dare speak
outline.gist: After ages of standing, people beg the prophets to intercede so judgment can begin; each declines, citing a small slip or, for Isa, what others made of him, saying Allah's anger that day is unlike any before or after.

outline.heading: Most tender toward His servants, yet beware
outline.gist: Allah is most kind to His servants, but whoever comes careless and unprepared is in danger; at the very least approach that day with deep reverence.

outline.heading: A nation that calls to good
outline.gist: Let there be a group that calls to good, enjoins what is recognised as beneficial and forbids what is recognised as harmful; ma'ruf and munkar are social terms that agree with Allah's teachings.

outline.heading: The whole ummah is that nation
outline.gist: Scholars read 'from among you' as the ummah of Muhammad within humanity, a general guide for Muslims at all times, while the next verse forbids being like those who split after clear proofs came.

outline.heading: Why the ummah cannot protect its own
outline.gist: We have examples of nations that ruined their unity with their own hands; the ummah lacks neither numbers, intellect, expertise nor youth, only unity and organisation, because it prefers to stroke its ego and prove itself right.

outline.heading: Divided despite the clearest book
outline.gist: If earlier nations were held to account for dividing with lesser scriptures, what of us with the clearest of books, who hunt for the small margin where we disagree as a reason not to work with or love one another?

outline.heading: Faces lit and faces darkened
outline.gist: Those who used faith to divide and shed blood will have dark faces and be told to taste the punishment for their ingratitude; on that day you must ask whether your face is lit or dark.

outline.heading: Bathing in His mercy forever
outline.gist: Those whose faces Allah lights up will bathe in His mercy for eternity, wave after wave, with never a dull moment in Paradise.

outline.heading: It comes down to the stands you took
outline.gist: The lit faces belong to those who stood clearly for what is beneficial and against what is harmful, kept their narrative clear and accepted the cost, rather than letting ego win.

outline.heading: Allah wants no injustice for anyone
outline.gist: These are Allah's verses recited in truth, and He intends no wrong to anyone in creation.

outline.heading: Not the fear we have of people
outline.gist: We fear people because they may be biased and take what is rightfully ours, but Allah has said no one in all creation will be wronged.

outline.heading: The nightmare of being treated fairly
outline.gist: What we truly fear is receiving exactly what we are owed, since we were counting on His generosity to overlook our weak sincerity, vanity, envy and love of being seen.

outline.heading: Two ways a child fears a father
outline.gist: Fear of mistreatment cannot coexist with love, but fear of disappointing someone can, and leads a child to say 'I know I was wrong, forgive me anyway'.

outline.heading: Worthy of His mercy, not deserving it
outline.gist: We come to Allah knowing we deserve nothing, loving Him and hoping we have done enough to be worthy of His mercy, the one goal of all our work.

3:152.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَكُمۡۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
3:152.en: Allah verily made good His promise unto you when ye routed them by His leave, until (the moment) when your courage failed you, and ye disagreed about the order and ye disobeyed, after He had shown you that for which ye long. Some of you desired the world, and some of you desired the Hereafter. Therefore He made you flee from them, that He might try you. Yet now He hath forgiven you. Allah is a Lord of Kindness to believers

3:153.ar: ۞إِذۡ تُصۡعِدُونَ وَلَا تَلۡوُۥنَ عَلَىٰٓ أَحَدࣲ وَٱلرَّسُولُ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ فِيٓ أُخۡرَىٰكُمۡ فَأَثَٰبَكُمۡ غَمَّۢا بِغَمࣲّ لِّكَيۡلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمۡ وَلَا مَآ أَصَٰبَكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
3:153.en: When ye climbed (the hill) and paid no heed to anyone, while the messenger, in your rear, was calling you (to fight). Therefor He rewarded you grief for (his) grief, that (He might teach) you not to sorrow either for that which ye missed or for that which befell you. Allah is Informed of what ye do

3:196.ar: لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ
3:196.en: Let not the vicissitude (of the success) of those who disbelieve, in the land, deceive thee (O Muhammad)

3:197.ar: مَتَٰعࣱ قَلِيلࣱ ثُمَّ مَأۡوَىٰهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ

24:11.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡۚ لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرࣰّ ا لَّكُمۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُم مَّا ٱكۡتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبۡرَهُۥ مِنۡهُمۡ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:11.en: Lo! they who spread the slander are a gang among you. Deem it not a bad thing for you; nay, it is good for you. Unto every man of them (will be paid) that which he hath earned of the sin; and as for him among them who had the greater share therein, his will be an awful doom

57:20.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱ وَزِينَةࣱ وَتَفَاخُرُۢ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَتَكَاثُرࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَوۡلَٰدِۖ كَمَثَلِ غَيۡثٍ أَعۡجَبَ ٱلۡكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُۥ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَىٰهُ مُصۡفَرࣰّ ا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَٰمࣰ اۖ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣱۚ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
57:20.en: Know that the life of the world is only play, and idle talk, and pageantry, and boasting among you, and rivalry in respect of wealth and children; as the likeness of vegetation after rain, whereof the growth is pleasing to the husbandman, but afterward it drieth up and thou seest it turning yellow, then it becometh straw. And in the Hereafter there is grievous punishment, and (also) forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure, whereas the life of the world is but matter of illusion

nYvcAvBUYrw.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 4: Quranic Themes, Avoiding Distractions
nYvcAvBUYrw.one_line: Distraction as the quiet ruin of good deeds: the lapse at Uhud, intimidation by the powerful, and people who want you as lost as they are.
nYvcAvBUYrw.summary: He presents distraction as the subtle danger for most Muslims: not a capital sin one consciously chooses but salt scattered across a life that slowly melts away its good deeds, fed by a nafs that procrastinates to avoid heavy truths like death and accountability, and by addictions that numb problems that seem too big. At Uhud the companions were winning until some, with a little love of this world in their hearts, left their post or fled; one lapse at a key moment cascaded into defeat and years of pain. Allah called the sorrow that followed a reward, settling the matter in this life, and the false news of the Prophet's death made the lost battle feel light. From this he teaches not to stay trapped grieving what passed or what one caused, but to repent and move on, and to fix on one goal with everything else as background noise. From 3:196-197 he warns not to be fooled or intimidated by the free movement and double standards of the powerful, since defeat comes only when one stops getting up. The Prophet's focus during the slander against Aisha is his model. From 4:27-28, Allah wants to turn to us and ease our way, while those lost in desire want company in their failure, though each will stand alone before Allah.

outline.heading: A theme throughout the Quran
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly warns against what wastes time, energy and capital, and against worldly desires that pull us away from our priorities.

outline.heading: Scattered salt: the slippery slope
outline.gist: Unlike murder or zina, which one knowingly chooses and can repent of, distraction is scattered everywhere like salt until it melts away all one's good deeds, and we rarely notice it eating up most of our lives.

outline.heading: The nafs as a master procrastinator
outline.gist: Capital sins are distant for most Muslims raised in Muslim homes, but Shaytan loves distraction; with an exam in three days the nafs suddenly wants to tidy the shelves, because facing mortality and accountability is heavy and distraction lets it run.

outline.heading: Addiction as escape
outline.gist: Addictions, whether substances, video games, screens or gambling, are the mechanism we use to forget a problem that feels too big to tackle.

outline.heading: Uhud: victory, then faltering
outline.gist: The second half of Aal Imran treats Uhud and its lessons; Allah kept His promise while the Muslims were routing the enemy, until they faltered, disputed and disobeyed after He showed them what they loved.

outline.heading: The archers leave the mountain
outline.gist: The first incident was the archers who ran down to the spoils and set off the cascade that followed.

outline.heading: Those who fled the battle
outline.gist: Once the enemy flanked them from behind the battle became chaotic, and some fled up the mountain, into the open land or back to Medina.

outline.heading: Some of you wanted this world
outline.gist: The Quran does not spare even the companions when there is a teachable moment: a small desire for worldly gain carried into a battle fought purely for Allah distracted them at a key moment, though Allah pardoned them.

outline.heading: Small lapses that cost dearly
outline.gist: That one mistake caused a domino effect of defeat and years of betrayal and killing of Muslims; it was no capital sin, just a distraction, which is exactly why such small things must be respected.

outline.heading: Running without turning to anyone
outline.gist: They fled into open land caring for no one, chasing spoils or escaping fear, while the Prophet stood at the rear calling the servants of Allah to come back.

outline.heading: Why sorrow is called a reward
outline.gist: Allah 'rewarded' them with sorrow upon sorrow rather than saying He punished them, since they were with the Prophet; the consequence came at once in this life, so the account was settled and they carry nothing further.

outline.heading: A bigger loss makes the smaller one light
outline.gist: Hearing that the Prophet had been killed, then learning he lived, made the lost battle and spoils feel trivial, the way news that your family is safe makes a burnt house bearable.

outline.heading: Do not grieve over what passed you by
outline.gist: The verse aims that we not grieve over what we missed or what struck us, since we do not know what would have been worse and Allah's decree was chosen for our good; dwelling on it traps us in the past.

outline.heading: Even when it was your fault
outline.gist: Uhud's suffering, seventy martyrs and the Prophet nearly killed, came from their own choices, yet a companion who lived forever thinking 'I am why Hamzah is gone' could never function; own the mistake, repent, and do not stay caught in it.

outline.heading: Zone in; everything else is background noise
outline.gist: Even outside religion, whoever lets secondary things distract him from his goal will keep failing; deal with each difficulty as it comes and get back on track, ignoring what people say.

outline.heading: The downfall of the great: a moment's lapse
outline.gist: For a split second the gold shone too brightly and everyone paid; the ruin of a great person is usually not a huge sin but a brief loss of focus or a waste of time dismissed as harmless.

outline.heading: Don't be fooled by their free movement
outline.gist: Do not be deceived by the disbelievers moving about the land as they please, like someone turning freely in bed, while you cannot protect your own land; letting this distract you locks you into a defeated mindset.

outline.heading: Double standards on display
outline.gist: We watch the powerful make and enforce laws and lift them at will, shamelessly applying them by race, religion and colour, deciding who is above the law and who is its target.

outline.heading: A brief enjoyment
outline.gist: Their joy is short-lived and their end is the worst outcome; treating status, power or wealth as goals shows we have not grasped Allah's power.

outline.heading: Power and wealth are means
outline.gist: Status, wealth and strength are only means to the real goals of unity, peace and a flourishing community; the display of others' power is Shaytan's way of making you feel defeated inside.

outline.heading: Defeat is a decision
outline.gist: A fighter who keeps getting up has not lost, and a game ends only when one side resigns; however strong the other side, whoever refuses to stay down will get his chance.

outline.heading: Keep walking toward justice
outline.gist: They parade their strength so you will stop speaking out and lose your goals; one person who keeps taking solid steps toward justice and freedom will arrive, and if he falls Allah brings another.

outline.heading: The Prophet's laser focus
outline.gist: Allah asks only for what you can do: keep walking toward your goal; nothing they said or did could distract the Prophet, who put out each fire with minimal effort and returned to his mission, so ask yourself what your goal is.

outline.heading: The slander, set aside for the mission
outline.gist: When his own wife was slandered he did not pursue it publicly while planning for battles, though Aisha felt it should have come first; the Quran itself settled the matter and declared her innocent.

outline.heading: Envy: hoping others fail
outline.gist: Shaytan, the nafs and people will all try to come between you and your objective; envy even makes us hope others fail at the impossible so we are not burdened by having been too lazy to try.

outline.heading: Marching steadily toward death
outline.gist: Life is play, adornment and competing for more; we are all walking toward death, resurrection and accountability, and anything not focused on that moment is a distraction.

outline.heading: Allah wants to turn to you
outline.gist: Allah wants to grant repentance to all His creation and has no interest in punishing anyone, so the burden is not on Him.

outline.heading: Those who want you as lost as they are
outline.gist: Followers of desire, masters of distraction, want you to drift so far you forget where the track was, like an unprepared student hoping the whole class fails or accusing a friend of studying behind his back.

outline.heading: You stand alone before Allah
outline.gist: You cannot bring your classmates into the court before Allah or plead that everyone did it; if there was a minority who did right, why were you not with them?

outline.heading: Obstacles we place before His will
outline.gist: If Allah wills to turn to us yet it does not happen, it is because we block it by letting the people of desire pull us off track.

outline.heading: Allah wants ease for you
outline.gist: Islam is meant to lighten life, not burden it, and it saddens him when people see it as hardship; Allah knows our innate weakness, so simply do not follow those who lead you astray.

outline.heading: The three distractions together
outline.gist: Desire for worldly things, intimidation by those who have more, and role models who live for money, sex and status all pull you from your direction; avoid them or they will be your ruin.

37:12.en: Nay, but thou dost marvel when they mock

37:13.en: And heed not when they are reminded

37:14.en: And seek to scoff when they behold a portent

37:15.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
37:15.en: And they say: Lo! this is mere magic

37:16.ar: أَءِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰ ا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ
37:16.en: When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we then, forsooth, be raised (again)

37:18.en: Say (O Muhammad): Ye, in truth; and ye will be brought low

37:19.ar: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجۡرَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَإِذَا هُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
37:19.en: There is but one Shout, and lo! they behold

37:20.en: And say: Ah, woe for us! This is the Day of Judgment

37:21.ar: هَٰذَا يَوۡمُ ٱلۡفَصۡلِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
37:21.en: This is the Day of Separation, which ye used to deny

37:22.ar: ۞ٱحۡشُرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَأَزۡوَٰجَهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡبُدُونَ
37:22.en: (And it is said unto the angels): Assemble those who did wrong, together with their wives and what they used to worship

37:23.ar: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهۡدُوهُمۡ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
37:23.en: Instead of Allah, and lead them to the path to hell

37:24.en: And stop them, for they must be questioned

37:25.en: What aileth you that ye help not one another

37:26.en: Nay, but this day they make full submission

37:27.en: And some of them draw near unto others, mutually questioning

37:11.ar: فَٱسۡتَفۡتِهِمۡ أَهُمۡ أَشَدُّ خَلۡقًا أَم مَّنۡ خَلَقۡنَآۚ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰهُم مِّن طِينࣲ لَّازِبِۭ
37:11.en: Then ask them (O Muhammad): Are they stronger as a creation, or those (others) whom we have created? Lo! We created them of plastic clay

2:216.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرۡهࣱ لَّكُمۡۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تُحِبُّواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَهُوَ شَرࣱّ لَّكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:216.en: Warfare is ordained for you, though it is hateful unto you; but it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said: O Adam! Inform them of their names, and when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth? And I know that which ye disclose and which ye hide

17:59.ar: وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرۡسِلَ بِٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ إِلَّآ أَن كَذَّبَ بِهَا ٱلۡأَوَّلُونَۚ وَءَاتَيۡنَا ثَمُودَ ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبۡصِرَةࣰ فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَاۚ وَمَا نُرۡسِلُ بِٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ إِلَّا تَخۡوِيفࣰ ا
17:59.en: Naught hindereth Us from sending portents save that the folk of old denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel - a clear portent save to warn

75:3.en: Thinketh man that We shall not assemble his bones

75:4.ar: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُۥ
75:4.en: Yea, verily. We are Able to restore his very fingers

9:25.ar: لَقَدۡ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةࣲ وَيَوۡمَ حُنَيۡنٍ إِذۡ أَعۡجَبَتۡكُمۡ كَثۡرَتُكُمۡ فَلَمۡ تُغۡنِ عَنكُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ ثُمَّ وَلَّيۡتُم مُّدۡبِرِينَ
9:25.en: Allah hath given you victory on many fields and on the day of Huneyn, when ye exulted in your multitude but it availed you naught, and the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for you; then ye turned back in flight
