4B7WFMg6MHI.speaker_note: second session of the sheikh's weekend tafseer of Al-Saffat; single voice
4B7WFMg6MHI.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 2: Verses 12-27
4B7WFMg6MHI.one_line: Mockers of Allah's signs, the resurrection by one compelling call, accountability when detained, and why submitting now beats submitting too late.
4B7WFMg6MHI.summary: He restates the surah's theme: contentment and obedience when we cannot see the wisdom, since we never truly know what is best for us. He criticises the community's superstition about jinn, which the Quran repeatedly says have no such power, and notes that paying exorcists while denying a child mental health support contradicts Allah's word. Verse 12 sets the believer's awe at human potential, shown when the angels bowed to Adam after he named things, against the disbelievers' mockery. Ordinary daily signs such as sunrise, birth and the cell are enough for faith; extraordinary miracles never helped earlier nations. Calling whatever one cannot explain 'sorcery' is the disbelievers' habit, like a doctor declaring every unexplained illness the work of jinn. The Quraysh's real objection was resurrection, because of what comes after it. One compelling call will raise everyone, on the Day of Recompense, and our tiny control over our own existence, down to our fingerprints, makes a second creation unremarkable for the One who made the first. The oppressors and their partners are detained because they are accountable. Truth is never decided by numbers, a lesson from Hunayn and the hadith of the foam, and Muslims today are fooled by their numbers. Everyone will submit; the only choice is whether to do it now, when it counts, rather than blaming others at the end.

outline.heading: Contentment with decrees we do not understand
outline.gist: The surah asks us to accept what Allah chooses even when we never learn why.

outline.heading: We do not know what is best for us
outline.gist: Our assessments of what helps us are guesses; trusting Allah means accepting ease and hardship alike.

outline.heading: The unseen listed in the first pages
outline.gist: Angels, tawhid and the stars' hidden link to the jinn, which the Quran says can learn nothing.

outline.heading: Jinn superstition against the Quran's clear word
outline.gist: Shaytan's power is whispering, which is real and harmful, yet people prefer myths of possession that keep exorcists in business while children go without mental health care.

outline.heading: Why the masjid fills in Ramadan
outline.gist: With devils chained, only the nafs remains to resist, which is why attendance is so much higher.

outline.heading: 'Bal': the real truth
outline.gist: After listing the unseen the surah moves to stories of prophets; bal negates what came before and affirms its opposite.

outline.heading: Not the strongest creation, but full of potential
outline.gist: Humans made of sticky mud are weaker than angels, yet human potential is the point of the story.

outline.heading: Adam and the names: why the angels bowed
outline.gist: The angels questioned placing humans on earth until Adam named, connected and articulated what they could not.

outline.heading: You marvel while they mock
outline.gist: The believer is in awe of the potential and the unseen around him; the disbelievers refuse to be reminded.

outline.heading: Rallying others to mock
outline.gist: Yastaskhirun: they seek to make mockery popular and recruit others to it.

outline.heading: No need for extraordinary miracles
outline.gist: The everyday signs are enough; if more were needed for iman, the Prophet would have brought them.

outline.heading: The Quran points to the real signs
outline.gist: Earlier nations rejected miracles; the Quran directs us to the sun, births, human achievement and the trillions of cells as the place to find Allah.

outline.heading: 'Clear sorcery': labelling what you cannot explain
outline.gist: Only disbelievers call the inexplicable sorcery; imagine doctors blaming jinn whenever they cannot diagnose an illness.

outline.heading: The believer accepts the decree and keeps seeking causes
outline.gist: Illness and loss are Allah's decree, not sorcery; the Prophet's transformation of people was what they called magic.

outline.heading: Resurrection was the real dispute
outline.gist: The Quraysh tolerated a god in the heavens but resisted resurrection because of the accountability that follows it.

outline.heading: Yes, and you will be humbled
outline.gist: The Prophet is told to answer that they will be raised in humiliation if unprepared.

outline.heading: One compelling call
outline.gist: The single blast explains the 'compelling ones' of the opening: everyone suddenly stands and looks at one another.

outline.heading: The Day of Recompense and Decision
outline.gist: Din means what you owe is delivered to you; the day settles every score and sorts people into two groups.

outline.heading: How little we control our own existence
outline.gist: Resurrection cannot be proven, but we do not run our organs, conception or seeds; we only arrange conditions.

outline.heading: He who compelled the first creation compels the next
outline.gist: He will restore even the lines of the fingertips, which we neither made nor control.

outline.heading: Gather the oppressors and their partners
outline.gist: Azwaj here means partners in crime, gathered with what they worshipped besides Allah.

outline.heading: Guided to the path of Hell
outline.gist: We ask for the straight path many times a day; those who refuse it find another path with a terrible end.

outline.heading: Detain them: they are accountable
outline.gist: Waqf means detention; one of the most quoted verses: we will be asked about our time, wealth, faculties and choices.

outline.heading: Why don't you help one another now?
outline.gist: Those who bullied the Prophet socially with numbers are mocked; truth was never found by the bigger crowd.

outline.heading: Hunayn: numbers that ran
outline.gist: The one time Muslims were impressed by their numbers, the earth closed in and the crowd fled.

outline.heading: Muslims fooled by their numbers
outline.gist: Feeling numerous, we do not unite or pool resources, while small groups work together; the hadith of the foam on the flood.

outline.heading: Submitting today, too late
outline.gist: On that day they are in full submission; everyone will submit, the only choice is when, while it still counts.

outline.heading: Submit now in what you do not understand
outline.gist: Islam must happen now; we know these scenes only because Allah tells them.

outline.heading: Turning to one another to blame
outline.gist: The first human reflex is to find someone to blame: parents, friends, then jinn, the perfect unmeasurable target.

outline.heading: The believer looks inward
outline.gist: A believer sees his own mistakes and accountability and accepts Allah's decree now, not too late.

outline.heading: Outro

DnCTUa6FjeY.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 1: Verses 1-11
DnCTUa6FjeY.one_line: Al-Saffat teaches submission to Allah in matters of the unseen and commands whose wisdom we cannot see, beginning with angels, tawhid and the guarded sky.
DnCTUa6FjeY.summary: He introduces Al-Saffat as the one surah devoted to obeying Allah in what we cannot see or do not understand. Every ruling has a purpose, but we are not entitled to know it; we obey because Allah commanded, and the benefit in His rulings is His generosity. Iman built on a scholar's ability to explain every ruling will collapse; it should rest on the constants of the universe, life, history and personal experience. Nuh built a ship far from water without asking why, and the human mind, which took Newton a lifetime to grasp gravity, cannot expect to comprehend everything; demanding that is arrogance. In verses 1-3 Allah swears by angels standing in perfect rows, driving creation where He wills, and reciting His remembrance, all known only through revelation, and he links their rows to straight prayer lines and to the unseen events of Ramadan. The answer to the oath is that your God is One, so you are accountable to Him alone and surrender your free will to no one else. Verses 6-10 describe the near sky adorned with stars that also guard against rebellious devils, which should end superstition, astrology and the community's obsession with jinn. Verse 11 asks whether humans, made of sticky clay, are stronger than these creations; our strength lies in the free choice to submit.

outline.heading: Opening
A cluster of surahs on obedience to Allah
outline.gist: Each surah of the cluster looks at submission from a different angle, because obedience is the core of the deen.

outline.heading: Interlude
The unique theme: obeying in the unseen and the unexplained
outline.gist: Al-Saffat alone addresses accepting what we cannot witness and following commands whose reasons we do not grasp, though every ruling serves an objective.

outline.heading: Being at peace with not knowing why
outline.gist: Some rulings and decrees will not be clear to us, and contentment with that is part of submission.

outline.heading: We obey because He is Allah
outline.gist: Refusing what a scholar cannot explain is unhealthy; we follow because Allah said so, and the wisdom in His rulings is His generosity, not our entitlement.

outline.heading: Nuh builds a ship far from any water
outline.gist: Nuh spent his life on a command he did not understand and asked no question, as other prophets in the surah will do.

outline.heading: Build iman on constants, not on explanations
outline.gist: Iman rests on observing the universe, life, history and experience; once Allah and the Prophet are accepted, the book is followed, and Allah only ever asked what benefits us.

outline.heading: He did not ask for all your wealth
outline.gist: Had Allah asked for everything, our stinginess would show; He asked only what benefits us and the community, so why do we not listen?

outline.heading: Comfort with our own ignorance
outline.gist: Claiming the right to understand everything is arrogance; Newton spent his life just to conclude that gravity exists.

outline.heading: Allah is unfathomable
outline.gist: If we could break Him down intellectually He would not be God; chasing unreachable knowledge costs us the knowledge we could have.

outline.heading: Recitation of the opening and its six-count madd
outline.gist: A recitation note on the long madd before a shaddah that opens the surah.

outline.heading: The oath by angels standing in rows
outline.gist: Allah swears by angels in perfect rows of worship, who will confess they never worshipped Him as He deserves, and of whom seventy thousand visit the heavenly House once ever.

outline.heading: Angels who drive creation
outline.gist: Zajirat means compelling something in a direction, understood as angels moving clouds and parts of the universe as Allah wills.

outline.heading: Repetition means perfection
outline.gist: The repeated word in Arabic emphasises that the angels do their work fully and perfectly.

outline.heading: Straight rows mirror equal hearts
outline.gist: Straightening prayer lines reflects brotherhood and equality; the physical mirrors the spiritual.

outline.heading: Angels reciting remembrance, known only by revelation
outline.gist: No journal tells us angels exist; we accept them on Allah's word.

outline.heading: The unseen events of Ramadan
outline.gist: Gates of Paradise opened, Hell closed, devils chained and a caller calling: we cannot sense them, but our spirits can grow sensitive to them.

outline.heading: Your God is One: accountable to One alone
outline.gist: The answer to the oath is the ultimate reality; no board or court has the right to question you as Allah does.

outline.heading: True freedom: surrendering free will only to Allah
outline.gist: Free will is given up to no person, not even the Prophet asked for it, only to Allah.

outline.heading: Lord of the points of light
outline.gist: A big ask comes with self-description; mashariq are the sources of light that ancient people waited for in the dark, and He is their caretaker.

outline.heading: The near sky: all we can observe
outline.gist: Dunya means near, not bad; everything our probes see is only the lowest sky.

outline.heading: Kawakib and the Arabs' desert sky
outline.gist: Every light in the sky besides the sun and moon is a kawkab; desert Arabs studied the clear night sky, and many stars still carry Arabic names.

outline.heading: Stars as adornment and as guards
outline.gist: The stars beautify the sky for us and also protect against rebellious devils, who cannot listen to the exalted assembly.

outline.heading: Eavesdropping ended with the Prophet
outline.gist: Before him devils brought scraps to sorcerers; the Quran repeatedly says this is no longer possible, yet the community is obsessed with jinn.

outline.heading: The snatcher pursued by a piercing flame
outline.gist: Any devil who snatches a word is destroyed at once by a piercing meteor, something we know only because Allah told us.

outline.heading: The cosmos is beyond our comprehension
outline.gist: A million light years means nothing to a mind that lives a hundred years; Ibrahim and the Prophet had to be shown it.

outline.heading: No room for astrology and superstition
outline.gist: Go by the clarity of the Quran over misused narrations; the stars' second function frees us from superstition.

outline.heading: Ask them: are they stronger, made of sticky clay?
outline.gist: On what basis does a creature of sticky mud object to the Almighty? Islam means accepting His word without objection.

outline.heading: Our strength is spiritual, not physical
outline.gist: Any wild animal is stronger than us; human power lies in freely choosing to obey Allah, drawing strength from Him rather than our clay.

Qv5kBPD_PsU.summary: He wants people to enter Ramadan with clear objectives. Working through the Prophet's sermon at the end of Sha'ban, he explains that Allah blesses chosen times, that Laylat al-Qadr compresses about sixty thousand nights into one, and that no voluntary act outweighs an obligation, while Ramadan multiplies both. Fasting is the central act: abstaining from lawful food by day should push you further from the red line of the forbidden, so lying, gossip and indecent viewing while fasting are absurd and strip the fast of its reward. An empty stomach slows the body so the spirit can reflect, which is why overeating at iftar defeats the month. Patience must be free of complaint, chosen hunger should build empathy for those with nothing at Maghrib, and the believer's provision grows because appreciation grows; he urges expecting little of others and much of oneself. Ramadan's culture is feeding others, illustrated by an old man in the Haram sharing his few dates. He closes with the five bounties to memorize and pursue: forgiveness of past sins, being freed from punishment through real competition, rewards Allah gives personally for fasting, Laylat al-Qadr sought across all the last ten nights, and dua that is not refused.

outline.heading: Clear objectives for the month
outline.gist: The aim is to strengthen intentions and enter Ramadan knowing the five rewards to work for.

outline.heading: Interlude
Salman's hadith: a month full of blessing
outline.gist: Every line of the hadith exists in authentic narrations, so his teachers narrated it; Allah singles out places and times for blessing, and Ramadan is among the most blessed.

outline.heading: Laylat al-Qadr: sixty thousand nights in one
outline.gist: A thousand months is about thirty thousand days, so the night holds the reward of some sixty thousand nights, far beyond the usual tenfold to seven-hundredfold.

outline.heading: Nothing outweighs the obligations
outline.gist: By the hadith qudsi nothing draws a servant closer than the obligations, while voluntary acts express love until Allah loves him; an obligatory prayer beats any amount of taraweeh.

outline.heading: Deeds multiplied, and fasting comes first
outline.gist: Any extra good deed in Ramadan equals an obligation outside it and each obligation equals seventy; the day's fast is obligatory and remains the most important act of the month.

outline.heading: The shepherd near the red line
outline.gist: Stay away from doubtful matters as a shepherd keeps his flock from the king's land; because people cannot always control their impulses, the religion includes preventive rulings.

outline.heading: Ramadan pushes you further from the line
outline.gist: By making even lawful food, drink and intimacy off limits, Ramadan moves your flock further from the forbidden.

outline.heading: Why the fast is in the day
outline.gist: As a child he wished Ramadan were at night, but the daytime fast is deliberate: it proves you need far less than you think and that there is more to you than appetite.

outline.heading: Abstaining from halal only to fall into haram
outline.gist: Leaving lawful food then lying, oppressing or acting on falsehood makes no sense; it does not invalidate the fast but removes its reward.

outline.heading: A fast that earns only hunger
outline.gist: Fast with excellence from everything forbidden and distracting, since some gain nothing from fasting but hunger and from night prayer but sore feet.

outline.heading: Haram to the power of two; more than a mammal
outline.gist: Sin becomes doubly forbidden in Ramadan; skipping lunch for Allah then watching indecency or gossip is senseless, because the month calls you beyond eating, drinking and reproducing.

outline.heading: Slowing the body so the spirit can notice
outline.gist: After hours of fasting, blood flow, metabolism and heart rate slow; like traffic forcing you to look at the scenery, this lets the spirit see Allah's beauty and provision.

outline.heading: The one creature that refuses food
outline.gist: A hungry healthy animal always eats; a fasting human declines, a choice that reveals the soul, but you must deliberately reflect to benefit.

outline.heading: The worst container is the stomach
outline.gist: The Prophet taught that no container is worse than a full belly and to leave a third for air; many traditions agree a full stomach blocks the spirit, and Ramadan jump-starts that path.

outline.heading: Month of patience without complaint
outline.gist: The patient enter Paradise without reckoning; patience must be beautiful like Yaqub's, accepting Allah's choice rather than whining through the thirty days.

outline.heading: 'I'm fasting' is no threat
outline.gist: Fasting should make you kinder and more empathetic, not a reason to snap at people or rage on the road.

outline.heading: Month of consolation: empathy needs imagination
outline.gist: Mercy depends on imagining another's pain, which is why people empathize readily with pain they have felt, like a bad back, and struggle with pain they have no parallel for.

outline.heading: Feeling the hunger of those with no iftar
outline.gist: Most people have never known real hunger; Ramadan lets them feel it by choice so they resolve that no child or family on a planet with enough food should sleep hungry.

outline.heading: Ramadan is about consuming less
outline.gist: You cannot stand in taraweeh on a full belly; break the fast with dates, water and soup, eat after, and learn that what you want and what you need are different.

outline.heading: Provision grows through appreciation
outline.gist: The paycheck does not grow; sitting hungry, you realize you could have lived without the means to feed your family, so what is in your account looks better.

outline.heading: Expect little from others, much from yourself
outline.gist: Life and marriage turn on expectations; demand more of yourself and less of others and of Allah, who has already given you so much.

outline.heading: It could have been worse
outline.gist: Patients in cancer clinics who cannot eat show what to be grateful for; pushing yourself is healthy, expecting Allah or others to do more is not.

outline.heading: A culture of feeding others
outline.gist: Giving iftar earns forgiveness without reducing the faster's reward; when two people break their fast together each should feed the other, a habit of selflessness.

outline.heading: The old man in the Haram with his dates
outline.gist: A frail elderly man who needed the food more than anyone walked around looking for someone, even a child, to share his dates and laban with.

outline.heading: Mercy, forgiveness and freedom from punishment
outline.gist: Whatever the authenticity of dividing the month into thirds, these three gifts frame Ramadan and lead into the five bounties.

outline.heading: Bounty one: forgiveness, and how the Prophet saw his sins
outline.gist: Nothing outweighs having your sins forgiven; the Prophet felt his smallest shortcomings weigh on his back and kept asking forgiveness though forgiven.

outline.heading: Fasting, night prayer and Laylat al-Qadr with faith
outline.gist: The believer feels sin like a mountain overhead; fasting, praying the nights, or standing on Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and hope of reward erases past sins.

outline.heading: A clean slate people would never give
outline.gist: People who forgive still keep you at arm's length, but Allah wipes everything and starts fresh, so do not carry the shame of past sins.

outline.heading: Bounty two: freedom from punishment is a competition
outline.gist: The chains of Jahannam are figuratively around every neck; Allah frees people every night of Ramadan, but millions compete, so bring your best, as the night you are freed outweighs any graduation or wedding.

outline.heading: Once freed, never taken back
outline.gist: Being freed does not mean you never sin, but that good outweighs evil and you always return; the term is the same as freeing a slave, and the Generous never revokes His gift.

outline.heading: Bounty three: the reward with no number
outline.gist: On the board of deeds every act has a number except fasting, which Allah rewards personally.

outline.heading: No Ramadan police; a day lost is lost
outline.gist: Only Allah sees whether you fast, and a day broken without excuse must be made up but its own reward is gone forever.

outline.heading: Bounty four: the night of status
outline.gist: The night Jibril first brought the Quran to the Prophet, when heaven spoke to earth, became the most valuable night of all time.

outline.heading: A lifetime in one night: don't gamble on the 27th
outline.gist: A thousand months is over 83 years of reward at once; Allah hid the night, so worship all of the last ten, because it is about quality, not quantity.

outline.heading: A Meccan surah before Ramadan existed
outline.gist: Most scholars hold Surah al-Qadr is Meccan, revealed before fasting was prescribed, so its first lesson was that one moment can outweigh a lifetime of mediocrity.

outline.heading: Jibril comes to see how the Quran is doing
outline.gist: On that night no punishment is decreed and Jibril descends to see whether the Quran is honoured, recited, loved and practised.

outline.heading: Bounty five: dua that is not refused
outline.gist: The fasting person's dua at iftar is not rejected and the dua verse sits in the middle of the fasting verses; keep the line to Allah open beyond Ramadan, trusting however He answers.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The whole lecture sets objectives for Ramadan through the hadith of Salman and the five bounties.

themes.label: Priorities in the deen: fundamentals before details
themes.note: Obligations carry more reward than any voluntary act; fasting is the most important act of the month.

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Fasting should move you further from the forbidden and the doubtful; sin while fasting is doubly wrong.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: An empty stomach slows the body so the spirit can reflect; a full belly blocks spiritual growth.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Beautiful patience means accepting Allah's choice without complaint; fasting should make you gentler.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Chosen hunger builds empathy for those who cannot break their fast and a resolve that no one should go hungry.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: Ramadan is meant to reduce consumption; overeating at iftar ruins taraweeh and the point of the month.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Provision increases through appreciation; expect little from others and much from yourself.

themes.label: Selfishness, greed of the soul (shuhh) and selflessness
themes.note: Ramadan's culture is feeding others first, even when hungry yourself.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Forgiveness of sins is the first and greatest bounty, a clean slate people never offer.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Being freed from the Fire is the second bounty, won through competition and never revoked.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Dua in Ramadan is promised acceptance; keep the connection open for life.

quran.point: A night better than a thousand months, worked out as about sixty thousand nights
The patient receive their reward without reckoning
Yaqub's beautiful patience as the model of patience without complaint
The burden of sin that weighed on the Prophet's back
The Prophet's past and future sins forgiven, yet he kept praying for forgiveness
Angels and Jibril descend and the night is peace
Allah is near and answers the caller, placed among the fasting verses

hadith.gist: Salman al-Farisi: on the last night of Sha'ban the Prophet addressed the people about the great blessed month, its night better than a thousand months, multiplied deeds, patience, consolation, increased provision and the reward of giving iftar
Hadith qudsi: My servant draws near to Me with nothing more beloved than the obligations, and keeps drawing near with voluntary acts until I love him and become his hearing and sight
The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear, with doubtful matters between, like a shepherd grazing near a preserve
Whoever does not abandon false speech and acting on it, Allah has no need of him leaving his food and drink
Many who fast get nothing but hunger and thirst, and many who pray at night get nothing but fatigue
The son of Adam fills no container worse than his stomach; a third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath
The believer sees his sin as a mountain about to fall on him; the hypocrite sees it as a fly on his nose
Whoever fasts Ramadan, prays its nights, or stands on Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and seeking reward has his past sins forgiven
Allah frees people from the Fire every night of Ramadan
Hadith qudsi: every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting; it is Mine and I reward it
Whoever breaks a day of Ramadan without excuse loses a reward that making it up does not restore
The fasting person has a dua at breaking the fast that is not refused

maxims: Ramadan slows the body so the spirit can notice
Haram becomes haram to the power of two
Because you're fasting, you behave better
What you want and what you need aren't the same
Expect little from others and much from yourself
It's never been about quantity, it's about quality

takeaways: Memorize the five bounties of Ramadan and keep them as your objectives
Fast from the forbidden as well as food: no lying, gossip or indecent viewing
Break your fast lightly so you can stand in taraweeh, and eat less overall
Expect less from others and more from yourself, and appreciate what you have
Feed others at iftar, seek Laylat al-Qadr in all of the last ten nights, and keep making dua

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said: O Adam! Inform them of their names, and when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth? And I know that which ye disclose and which ye hide

2:101.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمۡ رَسُولࣱ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُصَدِّقࣱ لِّمَا مَعَهُمۡ نَبَذَ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمۡ كَأَنَّهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:101.en: And when there cometh unto them a messenger from Allah, confirming that which they possess, a party of those who have received the Scripture fling the Scripture of Allah behind their backs as if they knew not

2:102.ar: وَٱتَّبَعُواْ مَا تَتۡلُواْ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلۡكِ سُلَيۡمَٰنَۖ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيۡمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ ٱلسِّحۡرَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَكَيۡنِ بِبَابِلَ هَٰرُوتَ وَمَٰرُوتَۚ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنۡ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَآ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ فِتۡنَةࣱ فَلَا تَكۡفُرۡۖ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنۡهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِۦ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡمَرۡءِ وَزَوۡجِهِۦۚ وَمَا هُم بِضَآرِّينَ بِهِۦ مِنۡ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمۡ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمۡۚ وَلَقَدۡ عَلِمُواْ لَمَنِ ٱشۡتَرَىٰهُ مَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِنۡ خَلَٰقࣲۚ وَلَبِئۡسَ مَا شَرَوۡاْ بِهِۦٓ أَنفُسَهُمۡۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:102.en: And follow that which the devils falsely related against the kingdom of Solomon. Solomon disbelieved not; but the devils disbelieved, teaching mankind magic and that which was revealed to the two angels in Babel, Harut and Marut. Nor did they (the two angels) teach it to anyone till they had said: We are only a temptation, therefore disbelieve not (in the guidance of Allah). And from these two (angles) people learn that by which they cause division between man and wife; but they injure thereby no-one save by Allah's leave. And they learn that which harmeth them and profiteth them not. And surely they do know that he who trafficketh therein will have no (happy) portion in the Hereafter; and surely evil is the price for which they sell their souls, if they but knew

2:142.ar: ۞سَيَقُولُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَا وَلَّىٰهُمۡ عَن قِبۡلَتِهِمُ ٱلَّتِي كَانُواْ عَلَيۡهَاۚ قُل لِّلَّهِ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقُ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبُۚ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
2:142.en: The foolish of the people will say: What hath turned them from the qiblah which they formerly observed? Say: Unto Allah belong the East and the West. He guideth whom He will unto a straight path

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: Thus We have appointed you a middle nation, that ye may be witnesses against mankind, and that the messenger may be a witness against you. And We appointed the qiblah which ye formerly observed only that We might know him who followeth the messenger, from him who turneth on his heels. In truth it was a hard (test) save for those whom Allah guided. But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain, for Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful toward mankind

2:144.ar: قَدۡ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجۡهِكَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبۡلَةࣰ تَرۡضَىٰهَاۚ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُونَ
2:144.en: We have seen the turning of thy face to heaven (for guidance, O Muhammad). And now verily We shall make thee turn (in prayer) toward a qiblah which is dear to thee. So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship, and ye (O Muslims), wheresoever ye may be, turn your faces (when ye pray) toward it. Lo! Those who have received the Scripture know that (this revelation) is the Truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do

2:145.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَتَيۡتَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِكُلِّ ءَايَةࣲ مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبۡلَتَكَۚ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِتَابِعࣲ قِبۡلَتَهُمۡۚ وَمَا بَعۡضُهُم بِتَابِعࣲ قِبۡلَةَ بَعۡضࣲۚ وَلَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتَ أَهۡوَآءَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِنَّكَ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:145.en: And even if thou broughtest unto those who have received the Scripture all kinds of portents, they would not follow thy qiblah, nor canst thou be a follower of their qiblah; nor are some of them followers of the qiblah of others. And if thou shouldst follow their desires after the knowledge which hath come unto thee, then surely wert thou of the evil-doers

2:146.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَعۡرِفُونَهُۥ كَمَا يَعۡرِفُونَ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡۖ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ لَيَكۡتُمُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:146.en: Those unto whom We gave the Scripture recognise (this revelation) as they recognise their sons. But lo! a party of them knowingly conceal the truth

2:147.ar: ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُمۡتَرِينَ
2:147.en: It is the Truth from thy Lord (O Muhammad), so be not thou of those who waver

2:148.ar: وَلِكُلࣲّ وِجۡهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَاۖ فَٱسۡتَبِقُواْ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِۚ أَيۡنَ مَا تَكُونُواْ يَأۡتِ بِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:148.en: And each one hath a goal toward which he turneth; so vie with one another in good works. Wheresoever ye may be, Allah will bring you all together. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

2:149.ar: وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:149.en: And whencesoever thou comest forth (for prayer, O Muhammad) turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship. Lo! it is the Truth from thy Lord. Allah is not unaware of what ye do

2:150.ar: وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حُجَّةٌ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِي وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتِي عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
2:150.en: Whencesoever thou comest forth turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship; and wheresoever ye may be (O Muslims) turn your faces toward it (when ye pray) so that men may have no argument against you, save such of them as do injustice - Fear them not, but fear Me! - and so that I may complete My grace upon you, and that ye may be guided

jVeX-bcJSs4.speaker: adnan
jVeX-bcJSs4.speaker_note: leads his annual Ramadan Quranic themes series at the centre, referring to the format he has used for five or six years
jVeX-bcJSs4.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 1: Quranic Themes, Having Direction
jVeX-bcJSs4.one_line: The qiblah as a direction for life: stewardship from Adam, superstition as lost direction, and the change of qiblah restoring purpose without needing oppression.
jVeX-bcJSs4.summary: He opens the series with the theme of having direction, treating the qiblah as both a physical and a figurative orientation. In Mecca oppression handed the Muslims a clear purpose, while in Medina comfort blurred it, and he warns against needing a victim narrative or a conspiracy to feel purposeful, noting how engagement surged during the bombing of Gaza and faded after, though the oppression continues. From the creation of Adam he argues that humans were destined for earth as stewards before Adam's first breath, set apart by the ability to articulate and learn, so stewardship is carried out through knowledge. From the people who threw their book behind their backs and followed Babylonian myths, he reads an escape from the hard work of responsibility, and applies it to Muslims who blame jinn, envy or magic rather than examining their own choices; he affirms the unseen and ruqyah but denies they explain our failures. The change of qiblah, revealed after Badr, restored purpose: a middle nation that witnesses to humanity and faces one house five times a day, whose life must face the same way. Comfort is a means, not the goal, and Ramadan breaks our routine to force that review.

outline.heading: Opening
Qiblah as direction in life
outline.gist: The word used for the direction of prayer also means having a purpose and knowing where your story is going; accepting Islam means never being lost in that sense.

outline.heading: Mecca had direction, Medina lost it
outline.gist: Oppression in Mecca gave the Muslims an automatic purpose: protect the faith and each other; in Medina, with no oppressor, they began to ask what they were there for, even questioning why they should go out to Badr.

outline.heading: Purpose does not require oppression
outline.gist: Al-Baqarah teaches that meaning does not depend on being oppressed; Muslims who need the world conspiring against them fall into a victim mentality, when in fact purpose is served far better without oppressors.

outline.heading: Gaza and purpose that fades
outline.gist: During fifteen months of bombing the mosques filled and the young came seeking Allah, then the pattern repeated and people went back to planning holidays; the oppression of the holy land has not ended, so even on those terms the work should continue.

outline.heading: Destined for earth before his first breath
outline.gist: Right after the Quran's introduction Allah tells the angels He is placing a steward on earth, not in Paradise, so Adam's destiny was always to be here and not the result of a mistake.

outline.heading: The angels' question
outline.gist: Having seen the jinn spread corruption, the angels ask why He would place on earth those who shed blood while they praise Him; He answers that He knows what they do not.

outline.heading: Teaching Adam the names: the gift of articulation
outline.gist: Allah taught Adam to name, describe and reason by analogy; shown unfamiliar things, the angels confess they know only what they were taught while Adam articulates and concludes, and they watch his mind at work.

outline.heading: The one creature that shapes its environment
outline.gist: Humans are not the largest, strongest or oldest creatures, but the only ones who organise and change their surroundings instead of adapting to them, which is why they were made stewards, one generation passing the baton to the next.

outline.heading: Stewardship through knowledge
outline.gist: Adam's first lesson was knowledge, so the more a person learns the better steward he becomes, making the earth a better place for people and a welcome habitat for every creature.

outline.heading: Those who threw the book behind their backs
outline.gist: Another people received the same responsibility, the sense of ownership that acts without waiting to be told, yet when a prophet came they threw Allah's book behind them as if they did not know.

outline.heading: Too much work: why they discarded it
outline.gist: The verse has many classical interpretations, but his reading is simple: guidance is exhausting work with no holiday until the grave, and the Prophet taught that every one of us is a shepherd responsible for his flock.

outline.heading: Following the devils' tales about Sulayman
outline.gist: They followed what the devils recited about Sulayman's kingdom, though he never disbelieved, along with Babylonian myths reaching back before Ibrahim, preferring easy superstition to clear guidance.

outline.heading: Why the myths are mentioned
outline.gist: No one truly knows who Harut and Marut were; the point is that leaving the clear stories and commands of the book for invented lore is how direction is destroyed and people are distracted from the book.

outline.heading: Jinn and envy, or our own mistakes?
outline.gist: Having lost direction, the ummah blames jinn, envy or magic whenever something fails rather than admitting it chose badly; he has seen highly intelligent people do this, while an honest check against the guidance shows the fault almost every time.

outline.heading: Real, but not the explanation
outline.gist: He does not deny jinn, magic or the evil eye, and urges reciting Quran over loved ones every night, but these do not drive the story of your purpose; children from stable homes may still develop mental illness, and one must not seek imaginary cures for problems with real ones.

outline.heading: Harm only by Allah's leave
outline.gist: What they learned only harmed them, and nothing touches a person except by Allah's will; a community that cannot hold itself accountable cannot grow, and fear of the unseen is where money is made and groups are controlled.

outline.heading: Ladders and broken mirrors
outline.gist: Western society had its own superstitions; the less direction a community has the more they spread, so Muslims should respect the unseen without blaming it and take every means needed for change.

outline.heading: Comfort in Medina and hope for a new qiblah
outline.gist: Free to practise openly and enjoying life with the Prophet, the companions lost focus, so he hoped for a change of qiblah that would mirror a change of direction, since in Islam every physical act has a figurative meaning.

outline.heading: The foolish ask why they turned
outline.gist: They had been facing the same direction as the Jews and Christians; people without knowledge would ask why the Muslims turned, and Allah answers that the east and the west are His and He guides whom He wills.

outline.heading: A middle nation, witnesses over humanity
outline.gist: The ummah is made a nation of balance between materialism and spirituality, desire and prohibition, so that humanity can see that this balance works.

outline.heading: Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque
outline.gist: Allah sees the Prophet looking up at the sky and grants him a qiblah he will be pleased with; wherever a Muslim is on earth he turns toward the Masjid al-Haram.

outline.heading: Each has a direction: race to good
outline.gist: Others will not follow your direction nor you theirs, because purposes differ; every person faces some direction, so compete in good deeds.

outline.heading: Wherever you are, never lost
outline.gist: The command to turn your face toward it wherever you go is repeated, so a Muslim dropped anywhere knows his direction physically and in life; being unsure what one lives for contradicts two whole pages of the Quran.

outline.heading: Every masjid is a satellite of His house
outline.gist: All mosques face the original house because we cannot all pray in Mecca; a house in Arabic also means a family, as when we say an aunt's house came to visit, so Allah's house is what we serve.

outline.heading: One unifying direction
outline.gist: Raising the hands in prayer is the same gesture as facing the Ka'bah during tawaf; tonight picture hundreds of millions of Muslims across the planet all facing the same point.

outline.heading: Facing the Ka'bah but living for something else
outline.gist: Facing the house of Allah five times a day while serving another cause in life is a contradiction that makes no sense.

outline.heading: Created for earth, not for the Garden
outline.gist: Al-Baqarah reminded the companions that they are stewards; the angels prostrated out of respect for the purpose they saw in Adam, who was made to be responsible on earth, not to remain in Paradise.

outline.heading: Harut, Marut and the age of astrology
outline.gist: Traced to their roots, the two names are names of planets, the moon and Jupiter, from the era of astrology; horoscopes only gain meaning in a life with no substance or direction.

outline.heading: Comfort is a means, not the goal
outline.gist: Revealed after Badr, the new qiblah brought the companions back to balance; we seek income, shelter and ease so we can serve our purpose, and when the means becomes the goal everything is lost.

outline.heading: Ramadan breaks the routine
outline.gist: Ramadan jams the wheels of routine and forces a person back to the drawing board to review why he lives and whether he still sees himself as Allah's witness to humanity.

outline.heading: The qiblah test: hard except for the guided
outline.gist: Facing Jerusalem in Mecca put Muslims beside all believers against idolatry; in Medina the mission became bringing the message to all humanity, a task of many lifetimes, so the change tested who would follow and who would turn back, and it is hard except for those Allah guides.

outline.heading: Outro

97:3.ar: لَيۡلَةُ ٱلۡقَدۡرِ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ أَلۡفِ شَهۡرࣲ‏
97:3.en: The Night of Power is better than a thousand months

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

15:29.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
15:29.en: So, when I have made him and have breathed into him of My Spirit, do ye fall down, prostrating yourselves unto him

2:186.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
2:186.en: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright

15:88.ar: لَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيۡنَيۡكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعۡنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ وَلَا تَحۡزَنۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱخۡفِضۡ جَنَاحَكَ لِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
15:88.en: Strain not thine eyes toward that which We cause some wedded pairs among them to enjoin, and be not grieved on their account, and lower thy wing (in tenderness) for the believers

AfUJU4QsM9A.speaker: adnan
AfUJU4QsM9A.speaker_note: Speaks as the imam of this masjid, addressing his own congregation on the eve of Ramadan.
AfUJU4QsM9A.title: A Ramadan Plan
AfUJU4QsM9A.one_line: On the eve of Ramadan: the month is where the seen and unseen meet, so starve the body a little, feed the spirit, and follow a plan.
AfUJU4QsM9A.summary: Delivered hours before the first night of Ramadan, this khutbah opens with the Prophet's sermon on the last day of Sha'ban and the hadith that the devils are chained when the month begins. The sheikh explains the month's status through the idea of two worlds: the seen and the unseen met when Jibril brought the Quran, and Ramadan is a yearly celebration of that book, the only living link between them since the Prophet's passing. Fasting follows from this. Because the month belongs to the unseen, we cut back on the hallmarks of the physical world (food, drink, intimacy, sleep) so the spirit, which Allah breathed into us and which no scan will ever image, can recover. With Shaytan restrained, we have thirty days to inspect the damage and rebuild our walls before the enemy returns. He points to the masjids that fill worldwide tonight as a call to the heart no organizer could match, and to 2:186 as Allah removing every middleman. The second khutbah gives a plan: a Quran target, taraweeh at the nearest masjid with your children, night and sunnah prayers, daily dhikr and dua, a daily lesson, and reconciling with people. He warns that disputes in a crowded masjid poison a night of prayer, and ends by saying that caring for Gaza starts with repentance.

outline.heading: Opening
The Prophet's sermon at the end of Sha'ban
outline.gist: Salman al-Farisi's narration, whose chain is disputed but whose content scholars accept: a great blessed month has come, with a night better than a thousand months, its fasting obligatory and its night prayer recommended.

outline.heading: The devils are chained on the first night
outline.gist: A second hadith: when Ramadan's first night arrives, the devils and the whispers they carry are shackled. He asks why the month has this status.

outline.heading: The last time the sky spoke to the earth
outline.gist: Ramadan marks the night Jibril, a creature of the unseen, brought the final revelation and began the story we belong to.

outline.heading: Stop where Allah's description of the unseen stops
outline.gist: We know the unseen only as far as Allah describes it, simply and briefly; speculating beyond the wording brings no gain.

outline.heading: Ramadan celebrates the Quran, the link that remains
outline.gist: The month draws its status from the book revealed in it (2:185). The companions called the Prophet's death their worst calamity, but the Quran on your shelf is still the link between the two worlds.

outline.heading: Why we fast: set the physical world aside
outline.gist: If the two worlds meet this month, reduce the hallmarks of biological life: food, drink, intimacy and sleep. You have eleven months for those.

outline.heading: Shaytan, the enemy who chose Hell, is restrained
outline.gist: Shaytan accepted Hell to make sure you lose, so treat him as an enemy (35:6). For thirty days Allah removes him, and everyone who has fasted feels the prayer is different.

outline.heading: A difference you feel but cannot measure
outline.gist: NASA has watched the sky every Ramadan and found no physical change, because the change happens on another level. You will still feel it.

outline.heading: Thirty days to rebuild your walls
outline.gist: Inspect the holes he made, repair your defences inside and out, and post archers at the gates so he finds no weakness when he is released. The gates of Hell are shut.

outline.heading: Open gates and a heart lifted above appetite
outline.gist: The gates of Paradise open so we can benefit. Put food down during the day; there is more to you than nourishment and desire, so let the spirit find its wings.

outline.heading: A turnout no election can match
outline.gist: A caller invites seekers of good to come forward. Elections struggle for turnout, yet tonight masjids in every country fill without anyone's effort, because Allah calls the hearts.

outline.heading: Soil and a breath from Allah
outline.gist: The body is soil that returns to the earth within a decade, but Allah breathed of His spirit into man (15:29), a phrase no one can explain.

outline.heading: No scan will find the spirit
outline.gist: Science will never image the soul, so do not circulate studies claiming to weigh it. Ignore that part of yourself long enough and it withers.

outline.heading: Not even 8% of the year for the soul
outline.gist: Ramadan revives the spirit by setting the body's needs aside for one month in twelve, so pray, supplicate, read and learn.

outline.heading: Not the best Ramadan, the best month of your life
outline.gist: Allah opened Paradise, closed Hell and removed your enemy, so come back to Him. He worries for anyone who dies without tapping into this other part of themselves.

outline.heading: Connecting beyond the physical
outline.gist: The spirit understands love, mercy, forgiveness and generosity. Setting intimacy aside by day teaches that connection exists beyond the body.

outline.heading: I am near: no middleman
outline.gist: In the middle of the fasting verses Allah answers directly that He is near and responds (2:186). Turning these nights into overconsumption wastes them.

outline.heading: Do not cheat the month
outline.gist: You can sleep all day and eat all night, but to leave changed, treat the month as the sky reaching out to you and open the link the Prophet left.

outline.heading: Interlude
A plan for Quran and prayer
outline.gist: Things work better with a plan: set a Quran target, pray taraweeh at the masjid nearest your home with your children following in a mushaf, add a few minutes of night prayer before Fajr, and keep the sunnah prayers.

outline.heading: A daily dhikr count and learning dua
outline.gist: Remember Allah a couple of hundred times a day, set time for dua, and teach your children to raise their hands and speak to Him. Dua is an art and a gift that takes practice.

outline.heading: Every person a student of knowledge
outline.gist: Listen daily to a teacher you benefit from and record one benefit a day. Fill the month with good deeds, each worth an obligatory act outside Ramadan.

outline.heading: Why voluntary worship still matters
outline.gist: Nothing matches an obligatory act, yet we pray the sunnah to admit to Allah that our quality and quantity fall short and to ask Him to overlook it.

outline.heading: Clear your heart of animosity
outline.gist: Call someone you have not spoken to in a long time and remove grudges, so the good habit outlasts the month.

outline.heading: Interlude
Disputes poison your prayers
outline.gist: A crowded masjid needs mercy and empathy. Every year a handful of ugly disputes spoil his month; humility toward fellow believers (15:88) is worth more than a night of prayer, and arriving late one night is fine.

outline.heading: From one khatm to seven
outline.gist: In 2013 one imam finished the Quran in London with barely a line behind him; now seven masjids complete it, a sign of the month's blessing and people's effort.

outline.heading: Caring for Gaza starts with yourself
outline.gist: Change for the Holy Land and the oppressed trickles out from here: if Gaza still pains you, begin with repentance and returning to Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Shaytan: his methods and how to resist him
themes.note: Shaytan chose Hell to make sure you lose. With him chained for thirty days, find the holes he made and fill them before he is released.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Humans are soil plus a spirit from Allah that no imaging tool will find. Neglected, it shrivels; fasting starves the body a little so the spirit can grow wings.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: In 2:186 Allah answers directly without telling the Prophet to relay it: I am near. In the plan, dua is an art and a gift to learn and teach children.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Everyone must be a student of knowledge at their capacity, even one recorded benefit a day from a teacher they like.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: In a crowded masjid, lowering your wing to fellow believers earns more than a night of prayer, while a dispute over space can poison it.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Change for the Holy Land trickles out from here; start by repenting and returning to Allah.

quran.point: Quoted within the hadith: the month holds a night better than a thousand months.
Allah defines Ramadan as the month in which the Quran was revealed, so the month's value comes from the book.
Shaytan is your enemy, so treat him as an enemy.
Allah breathed into man of His spirit; the phrase cannot be explained, but it means part of us is not of this world.
Placed in the middle of the fasting verses: Allah answers directly that He is near and responds, removing the middleman.
Lower your wing to the believers: humility toward fellow worshippers instead of fighting over space.

hadith.gist: The Prophet addressed the companions on the last day of Sha'ban: a great blessed month has come, with a night better than a thousand months; Allah made its fasting obligatory and its night prayer voluntary. He notes the chain is disputed but the content is not.

When the first night of Ramadan comes, the devils are chained, the gates of Hell are closed and none opened, the gates of Paradise are opened and none closed, and a caller says: seeker of good, come forward; seeker of evil, hold back.
A good deed done in Ramadan carries the reward of an obligatory act outside it.

takeaways: Write a Ramadan plan: a Quran target, daily dhikr count, daily dua, and one lesson of knowledge a day.
Pray taraweeh at the masjid nearest your home and bring your children with a mushaf to follow the imam.
Add night prayer before suhoor and the regular sunnah prayers; keep eating and sleeping in check so the month is not overconsumption.
Call someone you have not spoken to in a long time and clear any animosity from your heart.
Treat fellow worshippers with mercy and humility; a dispute over space can poison a night of prayer.
